  S3 --> S4["4. Release And Live Service\nPublication controls"]
  S4 --> S5["5. ADO Development Mesh\nPlaceholders then sync"]
  S5 --> S6["6. UAT And Hardening\nReal users"]
  S6 --> S7["7. Controlled ADO Triggers\nCreate/link dev work"]
  S7 --> S8["8. Reporting And Scale\nPower BI/Dataverse decision"]
```

## Stage 0 - Product Shape And Design

Purpose: make sure we are building the right product before adding deeper automation.

Key decisions:

| Decision | Why it matters | Preferred position |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Primary users | Drives screen layout and terminology. | Delivery/Governance Owner, Agent Owner / SME, Agent Builder / Developer. |
| Register lifecycle | Prevents ADO state confusion. | Keep register lifecycle separate from ADO state. |
| Gate model | Prevents false readiness. | DoR, DoD and production readiness are gates, not lifecycle stages. |
| Evidence model | Prevents URL-only governance. | Evidence needs summary, link, verifier and outcome. |
| MVP data platform | Affects build speed and future migration. | SharePoint Lists now, Dataverse-friendly schema later. |
| Visual design | Prevents fragile generated UI. | Follow v1 mockup pattern: operational hub, left navigation, lifecycle strip, guided panels. |
| ADO timing | Prevents the app becoming an ADO viewer too early. | Keep ADO as placeholders/hooks until delivery capture and gate flow are stable. |

Design review output:

- Confirm final MVP personas.
- Confirm screen map against the v1 mockups.
- Confirm lifecycle and gate wording.
- Confirm required fields by lifecycle and gate.
- Confirm which fields are editable in Power App versus later mirrored/triggered from ADO.

Status: **In progress.**

## Stage 1 - Data Foundation

Purpose: establish the structured data model.

Already done:

- Provisioned core SharePoint lists.
- Created child lists for readiness, knowledge, actions, ADO links, reviews and audit.
- Created sample agent and linked readiness checklist rows.
- Validated SharePoint list and column presence.

Remaining:

- Add real URL values to sample rows for link testing.
- Confirm field names against the latest dashboard/register thinking.
- Decide if any missing v0.3 governance fields need to be added before app hardening.
- Confirm evidence library/folder pattern.

Exit criteria:

- One representative agent can be captured with child evidence rows.
- All mandatory MVP fields exist.
- List names and column names are stable enough for app formulas and flows.

Design checkpoint:

Do not build deeper automation until field ownership and required fields are agreed.

## Stage 2 - Power App MVP

Purpose: create a usable governance workspace.

Already done in prototype:

- Dashboard with agent metrics.
- Agent row open navigation.
- Agent detail with section tabs.
- Readiness checklist status updates.
- Action creation.
- Explicit clickable launch buttons for known URL fields.

MVP screen map, guided by v1 mockups:

| Screen / area | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Home dashboard | Executive and delivery-orchestration view of lifecycle counts, attention items and portfolio split. |
| Pipeline board | Kanban-style lifecycle view where movement is constrained by gate readiness. |
| Register | Search, filter and open active agent records. |
| Intake | Guided multi-step capture from idea through scope, knowledge, gate check and submit/promote. |
| Agent detail / Template | Main agent dossier, template completion and lifecycle context. |
| Gate review | Structured DoR, DoD and production readiness decision capture. |
| Knowledge | Knowledge source and evidence capture. |
| Testing | Test questions, UAT evidence and outcomes. |
| Publishing / AIS Review | AIS outcome, publication readiness, beta testers, publish date and decision actions. |
| Reports | Exception and readiness reporting. |
| Admin/config | Read-only config visibility, later admin-only management. |

UX rules from prototype learning:

- Use real buttons for actions.
- Do not hide primary workflows below the visible canvas.
- Use tabs or clear navigation for major sections.
- Use tooltips on controls whose effect is not obvious.
- Use explicit `Open` buttons for external links.
- Do not rely on label click behavior for important interactions.

Exit criteria:

- Three personas can complete the day-in-the-life flow with one representative agent.
- No core action depends on obscure canvas scrolling.
- App checker issues are reviewed and accepted or fixed.

Design checkpoint:

Pause after the create/edit and gate review screens. Validate terminology and workflow before building release/live-service controls.

## Stage 3 - Gate And Lifecycle Control

Purpose: make the Power App the delivery orchestrator, not just an information display.

Deliverables:

- Gate review screen.
- Lifecycle movement controls.
- Required-field checks.
- Blocking messages with next actions.
- Promotion decision rows.
- Change log rows for movement and gate decisions.
- Pipeline board movement rules.

Rules:

- No stage movement if required evidence is missing.
- DoR must guide what is needed before build starts.
- `Passed with conditions` must require conditions and an action.
- AIS evidence can support a decision but cannot automatically pass gates.
- Governance decision history must be visible.

Exit criteria:

- DoR, DoD and production readiness can be formally reviewed.
- App blocks movement when required rows are incomplete.
- Every decision has date, approver, outcome and supporting evidence.

Design checkpoint:

Review gate wording with the Delivery/Governance Owner before enforcing rules too strictly.

## Stage 4 - Release And Live Service

Purpose: make publication and production movement safe.

Deliverables:

- Publishing / AIS Review screen.
- Release evidence panel.
- Production group capture separate from UAT users.
- Rollback readiness.
- Comms readiness.
- DLP / connector review.
- ELS status.
- Monitoring link.
- Support route.
- Next service review date.

Exit criteria:

- Agent cannot move to `Live / Monitor` without production readiness evidence.
- Live agents show support, monitoring, review date and open service exceptions.
- Dashboard reports live-service gaps.

Design checkpoint:

Confirm service ownership model and production group terminology before building too much UI around it.

## Stage 5 - ADO Development Mesh

Purpose: connect ADO after the Power App delivery flow is stable.

ADO is the development execution space: user stories, issues, bugs, developer tasks and technical release work. The Power App should orchestrate the overall agent delivery and show ADO evidence only where useful.

Deliverables:

- ADO placeholders in the Delivery/Development tab.
- ADO export/sync script or Power Automate flow.
- Populate `Agent ADO Links`.
- Populate ADO mirror fields on `Agents`.
- Populate `Sync Audit`.
- Add manual "refresh delivery links" pattern if feasible.

Power App should show:

- ADO work item ID.
- Work item type.
- State.
- Assigned to.
- Changed date.
- URL.
- Relationship type.

Rules:

- ADO mirrored fields are read-only in the Power App unless a later explicit trigger is designed.
- ADO state must not automatically approve governance gates.
- Sync failures must be visible.

Exit criteria:

- Delivery tab shows real ADO links for at least one agent.
- Sync audit has successful and failed run visibility.
- No lifecycle state changes happen automatically from ADO.

Design checkpoint:

Confirm which ADO work item types belong in the register view first: likely `User Story` / backlog item, `Bug`, `Task`, `Issue`, and any agent-level work item used by the development team.

## Stage 6 - UAT And Hardening

Purpose: make the app dependable for real users.

Deliverables:

- UAT script for three personas.
- Accessibility pass.
- Performance pass.
- Permissions test.
- Data quality report.
- App checker issue log.
- Admin/support guide.

Exit criteria:

- Agent Owner / SME can update evidence and actions.
- Agent Builder / Delivery Lead can understand delivery expectations and links.
- Governance Owner can review gates and exceptions.
- Permission model prevents accidental edits to mirrored or restricted fields.

Design checkpoint:

Review whether SharePoint Lists are still sufficient. If relationships, permissions, or reporting are becoming too heavy, evaluate Dataverse before wider rollout.

## Stage 7 - Controlled ADO Triggers

Purpose: add explicit ADO creation/linking after read-only sync is trusted.

Possible triggers:

- Create ADO development story/task from approved delivery requirement.
- Create ADO `Bug` or `Issue` from a gate blocker, failed test or live-service problem.
- Link existing ADO work to the agent delivery record.
- Add governance summary link back to ADO.

Rules:

- Every write-back is user-triggered.
- Every write-back writes an audit row.
- Failed write-back must not lose Power App data.
- No broad bidirectional sync until ownership rules are proven.

Exit criteria:

- Created ADO work item ID and URL return to the register.
- Sync audit records success/failure.
- Users understand which system owns which fields.

## Stage 8 - Reporting And Scale

Purpose: decide how the product grows beyond MVP.

Options:

| Area | Option |
| --- | --- |
| Reporting | Power App dashboard, Power BI, or both. |
| Data platform | Continue SharePoint Lists or move to Dataverse. |
| ALM | Manual export/import, solution packaging, or fuller pipeline. |
| Governance | Extend to more agent types, teams or portfolios. |

Exit criteria:

- Roadmap for production support is agreed.
- Ownership and support model is documented.
- Data retention and audit expectations are confirmed.

## Near-Term Plan

The next work should not be more random feature addition. Recommended order:

1. Review `docs/25-screen-map-and-lifecycle-capture-matrix.md`.
2. Confirm product label: `Agent Delivery Hub` for app chrome and `Agent Register` for the data/register view.
3. Confirm the left-navigation screen map and lifecycle wording.
4. Confirm the DoR capture journey: what information must be gathered before build starts.
5. Rerun Graph provisioning to add v27 template columns to `Agents`.
6. Run Graph validation and confirm the new columns exist.
7. Bind the Template tab to the new User Story, Instructions, Topics, Acceptance Criteria, Build Notes and Release Notes fields.
8. Add real sample URLs to SharePoint and confirm all link controls are clickable.
9. Add schema-backed Test Questions editing in the app.
10. Tighten visual density and typography across Home, Detail and Pipeline.
11. Keep ADO placeholders visible but defer ADO sync until the delivery flow is stable.

## Design Questions To Answer Next

| Question | Decision needed |
| --- | --- |
| Who is the primary user of the dashboard: delivery orchestrator, governance owner, executive or agent owner? | Drives dashboard density and metrics. |
| Should the product name be Agent Register or Agent Delivery Hub? | Drives user expectation and navigation language. |
| Should one screen contain all agent detail, or should gate/release/live service become separate screens/tabs following the mockups? | Drives navigation architecture. |
| Which fields are mandatory for each lifecycle stage? | Drives validation. |
| What exactly must DoR capture before build starts? | Drives the intake/template forms. |
| Should readiness checks be reusable templates copied per agent, or live config rows linked to agents? | Drives data maintenance. |
| Where should evidence folders be created: manually, script, or flow? | Drives evidence UX. |
| What ADO work items should appear only as placeholders first? | Keeps ADO excluded while preserving future hooks. |
| What does "ready enough for MVP" mean for visual polish? | Drives time spent on UI before integration. |

## Roadmap Status Summary

| Stage | Status |
| --- | --- |
| 0. Product shape and design | In progress |
| 1. Data foundation | Mostly done for prototype |
| 2. Power App MVP | Prototype started; core screens incomplete |
| 3. Gate and lifecycle control | Partially prototyped |
| 4. Release and live service | Not started |
| 5. ADO development mesh | Placeholder only |
| 6. UAT and hardening | Not started |
| 7. Controlled ADO write-back | Not started |
| 8. Reporting and scale | Not started |

# 09 - Agent Register Build Specification

Date: 2026-05-29

Status: Draft v0.1

## Purpose

This specification turns the Agent Register operating model into a buildable solution across Power Platform, SharePoint and Azure DevOps.

The design principle is:

**Power App controls movement. Azure DevOps executes work. SharePoint stores evidence. Power Automate keeps the mesh current.**

The first build should create a governed Agent Register that gives service, governance and delivery teams one controlled view of agent readiness without forcing developers to manage delivery work inside the Power App.

## Inputs

This specification is based on:

- The v1/v2 Agent Delivery Hub build pack now stored under `software/v1/agent_delivery_hub_build_pack`.
- The Azure DevOps AS-IS baseline for the `Copilot Studio Agents` project.
- `docs/06-ado-baseline-analysis.md`.
- `docs/07-powerapp-ado-mesh-schema.md`.
- `docs/08-ado-powerapp-operating-model-proposal.md`.
- The later `Agents Register - Diagram Aligned Executive Dashboard v0.3` thinking, where the register becomes a governance control ledger.

## Confirmed Environment Assumptions

| Area | Assumption |
|---|---|
| Power Platform | You have access to create or update a Canvas Power App and Power Automate flows. |
| SharePoint | You have access to a SharePoint site where Microsoft Lists and evidence folders can be created. |
| Azure DevOps | You have access to the `Ofgem-DDaT` organisation and `Copilot Studio Agents` project. |
| ADO project ID | `1406a8ae-4bb0-4c80-acca-c6dcb5e07ef3`. |
| ADO process | `AI_agent_delivery`. |
| ADO teams seen | `Agent Ideas`, `Copilot Studio Agents Team`. |
| ADO work item types in use | Includes `Idea`, `Agent`, `Portfolio`, `Feedback`, `Product Backlog Item`, `Bug`, `Task`. |
| Evidence store | SharePoint document libraries or folders linked from register rows. |
| First integration posture | Read-only ADO sync first, then controlled write-back after ownership rules are proven. |

## Scope

### In Scope For The First Build

- SharePoint/Microsoft Lists data model for the Agent Register.
- Canvas Power App for dashboard, register, template detail, gates, delivery links, release evidence and live-service controls.
- Power Automate flows to sync selected Azure DevOps work item data into SharePoint lists.
- Controlled evidence capture: summaries, links, approvers, dates, decisions and actions.
- Read-only ADO delivery visibility in the Power App.
- Lifecycle and gate rules that enforce "no register update, no stage movement".
- Basic reporting views for portfolio control and delivery/governance exceptions.

### Out Of Scope For The First Build

- Full Dataverse replacement.
- Fully bidirectional ADO synchronization.
- Rebuilding Azure DevOps Boards in Power Apps.
- Managing sprint execution, tasks and bugs inside the Power App.
- Automated production approval without human gate review.
- Replacing existing Power Platform ALM or Azure DevOps release processes.

## Target Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph Experience["Experience Layer"]
    PowerApp["Power App\nAgent Register workspace"]
    ADOBoards["Azure DevOps Boards\nDelivery workspace"]
    Teams["Teams\nNotifications and collaboration"]
  end

  subgraph Governance["Governance Control Layer"]
    Agents["Agents list\nGoverned control record"]
    Template["scrAgentTemplate\nFull agent dossier"]
    Gates["Gate reviews\nDoR, DoD, production readiness"]
    Actions["Actions and exceptions"]
  end

  subgraph Delivery["Delivery Execution Layer"]
    Idea["ADO Idea"]
    AgentWI["ADO Agent"]
    Work["ADO Feature, PBI, Task, Bug, Feedback"]
    Release["ADO pipeline and release evidence"]
  end

  subgraph Integration["Integration Layer"]
    Flows["Power Automate flows"]
    AdoLinks["Agent ADO Links list"]
    SyncAudit["Sync Audit list"]
  end

  subgraph Evidence["Evidence And Service Layer"]
    Docs["SharePoint evidence library"]
    Knowledge["Knowledge Sources list"]
    Monitoring["Monitoring and service review links"]
    Support["Support route and ELS controls"]
  end

  PowerApp --> Agents
  PowerApp --> Template
  PowerApp --> Gates
  PowerApp --> Actions
  ADOBoards --> Idea
  ADOBoards --> AgentWI
  ADOBoards --> Work
  ADOBoards --> Release
  Flows --> AdoLinks
  Flows --> SyncAudit
  Idea --> Flows
  AgentWI --> Flows
  Work --> Flows
  Release --> Flows
  Agents --> AdoLinks
  Template --> Knowledge
  Gates --> Docs
  Agents --> Monitoring
  Agents --> Support
  Teams --> PowerApp
  Teams --> ADOBoards
```

## System Responsibilities

| System | Owns | Mirrors or references | Must not become |
|---|---|---|---|
| Power App Agent Register | Governance state, gate decisions, evidence summary, ownership, movement, service readiness and live controls. | ADO work item IDs, states, owners, links and release evidence. | A sprint board or developer task manager. |
| SharePoint Lists | Structured register data, child rows, configuration tables and audit rows. | Selected ADO fields via sync. | A hidden spreadsheet with uncontrolled state changes. |
| SharePoint Documents | Evidence files, supporting material, screenshots, sign-offs and exported reports. | Linked from register evidence fields. | The workflow engine. |
| Azure DevOps | Delivery execution, work item hierarchy, defects, feedback, repos, pipelines and release mechanics. | Power App register link and governance status where needed later. | The full governance dossier. |
| Power Automate | Scheduled sync, notifications, audit entries and controlled ADO creation/linking. | ADO REST API responses and SharePoint list changes. | An invisible approval engine with no audit trail. |

## Lifecycle Model

The register lifecycle is intentionally separate from ADO board states.

| Register lifecycle | Meaning | Main gate or control |
|---|---|---|
| Intake / Capture | Idea is recorded and shaped. | Minimum intake fields. |
| Evaluate | Business, governance and delivery value are reviewed. | Approval decision. |
| Approve | Accepted for controlled delivery. | Approval conditions captured. |
| Ready / Design | User story, instructions, knowledge and ownership are prepared. | Definition of Ready. |
| Build & QA | Delivery work proceeds in ADO. | ADO delivery links and defects visible. |
| Private Beta / UAT | Users test the agent before production use. | Definition of Done and UAT outcome. |
| Live / Monitor | Agent is live and under service control. | Production readiness, release evidence, ELS and monitoring. |
| Blocked | Movement is stopped. | Blocking action required. |
| Parked / Backlog | No active delivery movement. | Review date or reactivation trigger. |

DoR, DoD and production readiness are gates, not lifecycle stages.

| Gate | Purpose | Typical owner |

| Definition of Ready | Confirms enough business, design, knowledge and ownership evidence exists to start build. | Governance Owner with Agent Owner and Builder input. |

# 07 - Power App And Azure DevOps Mesh Schema

## Design Intent

Azure DevOps and the Power App should not duplicate each other.

Azure DevOps should stay close to development and delivery execution. The Power App should become the governed Agent Register and template-first visibility layer.

The integration should work as a mesh:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  ADO["Azure DevOps\nDelivery execution"] --> Sync["Mapping / sync layer"]
  PowerApp["Power App\nAgent Register governance"] --> Sync
  Sync --> ADOFields["ADO mirror fields\nIDs, states, links"]
  Sync --> Lists["Microsoft Lists\nAgent detail, evidence, reviews"]

  ADO --> Repo["Git repo / solution export"]
  ADO --> Release["Dev -> UAT -> Prod release"]
  PowerApp --> Template["scrAgentTemplate"]
  Template --> Evidence["Knowledge, tests, checklist,\npromotion decisions, actions"]
```

## Proposed Data Ownership

| Domain | Owns the record | Mirrors |
|---|---|---|
| Agent identity | Power App `Agents` list | ADO `Agent` work item ID, URL and state |
| Idea intake | ADO `Idea` initially, or Power App intake if business-facing | Linked Agent Register row once accepted |
| Delivery work | ADO `Feature`, `Product Backlog Item`, `Task`, `Bug` | Summary counts and links in Power App |
| Governance evidence | Power App child lists | ADO can link to evidence, but should not duplicate repeatable rows |
| Deployment status | ADO release/pipeline/repo signals | Power App displays latest known environment URLs and dates |
| Portfolio | Shared controlled vocabulary | Power App list should align to ADO `Portfolio`/custom field |

## Proposed Microsoft Lists Schema

### Agents

The `Agents` list remains the main register and `scrAgentTemplate` source.

Add or confirm these ADO mesh fields:

| Field | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `AdoProjectId` | Text | Stable ADO project ID. |
| `AdoProjectName` | Text | Human-readable project. |
| `AdoAgentWorkItemId` | Number | Linked ADO `Agent` work item. |
| `AdoAgentUrl` | Hyperlink | Direct link to the ADO work item. |
| `AdoIdeaWorkItemId` | Number | Source `Idea` work item where relevant. |
| `AdoState` | Text | Read-only mirror of current ADO state. |
| `AdoWorkItemType` | Text | Usually `Agent`. |
| `AdoAssignedTo` | Text or Person | Delivery owner mirror. |
| `AdoAreaPath` | Text | ADO area path. |
| `AdoIterationPath` | Text | ADO iteration path. |
| `AdoChangedDate` | DateTime | Last ADO change seen by sync. |
| `AdoSyncStatus` | Choice | Synced, Missing ADO link, Conflict, Error. |
| `AdoSyncNotes` | Note | Human-readable sync issue or mapping note. |

### Agent ADO Links

Use this if one agent can have many ADO work items.

| Field | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `Title` | Text | Link title. |
| `Agent` | Lookup to Agents | Register row. |
| `AdoWorkItemId` | Number | Linked work item ID. |
| `AdoWorkItemType` | Text | Idea, Agent, Feature, Task, Bug, Feedback. |
| `AdoState` | Text | Current state. |
| `AdoUrl` | Hyperlink | Direct link. |
| `RelationshipType` | Choice | Source idea, delivery epic, feature, task, bug, feedback, dependency. |
| `Direction` | Choice | ADO to Power App, Power App to ADO, bidirectional reference only. |
| `LastSeen` | DateTime | Sync audit. |

### ADO Boards

| Field | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `Title` | Text | Board name. |
| `TeamName` | Text | Team owning the board. |
| `BoardId` | Text | ADO board ID. |
| `Purpose` | Choice/Text | Ideas, Agents, Portfolios, Features, Backlog. |

### ADO Board Columns

| Field | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `Title` | Text | Column name. |
| `Board` | Lookup | Parent board. |
| `ColumnType` | Text | Incoming, inProgress, outgoing. |
| `ItemLimit` | Number | WIP limit. |
| `StateMappingsJson` | Note | Raw mappings by work item type. |

### ADO Work Item Types

| Field | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `Title` | Text | Type name. |
| `ReferenceName` | Text | ADO reference. |
| `Category` | Choice | Delivery, governance, test, feedback, portfolio. |
| `UseInPowerApp` | Yes/No | Whether the type is surfaced in the Agent Register. |

### ADO Work Item States

| Field | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `Title` | Text | State name. |
| `WorkItemType` | Lookup/Text | Parent work item type. |
| `StateCategory` | Text | Proposed, InProgress, Resolved, Completed, Removed. |

| Testing and UAT | `Custom_CSA_TestQuestions`, `Custom_CSA_UatTesters` |

## Delivery/Governance Overlap

Azure DevOps is currently carrying both:

- Delivery execution: backlog, features, tasks, bugs, deployments, releases, development work and repo movement.
- Governance evidence: idea evaluation, knowledge readiness, PII, test questions, UAT testers, agent instructions and lifecycle maturity.

That overlap is not wrong, but it needs a clear boundary. Otherwise the same information will drift between Azure DevOps and the Power App.

## Recommended Boundary

| Concern | Recommended source of truth |
|---|---|
| Agent catalogue and executive visibility | Power App / Microsoft Lists |
| Agent detail template completion | Power App / Microsoft Lists |
| Knowledge sources as repeatable governed rows | Power App / Microsoft Lists |
| Test questions as repeatable rows | Power App / Microsoft Lists |
| Readiness checklist and promotion review | Power App / Microsoft Lists |
| Build backlog, task execution and bugs | Azure DevOps |
| Repo, solution export/import and release mechanics | Azure DevOps |
| Current delivery state mirror | Azure DevOps -> Power App |
| Agent lifecycle governance status | Power App, with mapped ADO signal |

## Project-Scoped Work Item Sample

The second export, `exports/ado-baseline-20260529-125549`, fixed the WIQL sample query:

```wiql
WHERE [System.TeamProject] = 'Copilot Studio Agents'
```

That means the 50 sampled work items are now all from `Copilot Studio Agents`.

|---|---:|
| `Feedback` | 12 |
| `Idea` | 11 |
| `Portfolio` | 8 |
| `Agent` | 7 |
| `Product Backlog Item` | 7 |
| `Bug` | 4 |
| `Task` | 1 |

|---|---:|

| `Ready` | 5 |

| `One For The Future` | 1 |
| `To Do` | 1 |
| `Completed` | 1 |
| `Evaluating` | 1 |

| Area path | Count in sample |
|---|---:|

| `Copilot Studio Agents\Agent Ideas` | 19 |

|---|---:|
| `ArtifactLink` | 117 |
| `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy-Reverse` | 35 |
| `System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy-Forward` | 35 |
| `System.LinkTypes.Related` | 14 |

The sample confirms that this is not a simple backlog. It contains:

- Live agent lifecycle records: 7 sampled `Agent` items, all currently in `Testing`.
- A substantial intake/evaluation lane: 11 sampled `Idea` items across `Ready`, `Ready With Conditions`, `One For The Future`, `Completed` and `Evaluating`.
- Operational feedback and defects: 12 `Feedback` and 4 `Bug` items.
- Delivery support work: PBIs and tasks.
- Portfolio records in the same project.

This strengthens the recommendation that Power App should present an integrated register view while Azure DevOps remains the execution system.

### Fields Actually Populated In The Sample

The sampled work items show useful data already populated in ADO:

| Theme | Populated sample fields |
|---|---|
| Agent metadata | `Custom_CSA_AgentName`, `Custom_CSA_AgentSummary`, `Custom_CSA_AgentModelUsed`, `Custom_CSA_SolutionName` |

The initial 50-work-item sample in `exports/ado-baseline-20260529-110559` is not reliable as a project-only sample. It included work items from other projects because the original WIQL did not filter on `System.TeamProject`.

Use `exports/ado-baseline-20260529-125549` for project-scoped work-item sample analysis.

# 03 - Power App / Microsoft Lists Model

## Design stance

Use Microsoft Lists as the initial practical storage layer, but avoid building one overloaded list.

The app needs enough structure to keep Azure DevOps metadata, agent details and template-driven visibility aligned.

## Suggested lists

| List | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Agent Register | Main agent catalogue. |
| Agent Details | Extended template/detail sections. |
| Agent Lifecycle | Lifecycle/status history. |
| ADO Projects | Azure DevOps project records. |
| ADO Teams | Teams from Azure DevOps. |
| ADO Boards | Boards from Azure DevOps. |
| ADO Fields | Field catalogue, including custom fields. |
| ADO Work Item Types | Epic, Feature, User Story, Bug, Task, custom types. |
| ADO Areas | Area Path hierarchy. |
| ADO Iterations | Iteration/sprint hierarchy. |
| ADO Work Items | Optional synced records from Azure DevOps. |
| Field Mapping | Maps ADO fields to app fields. |
| Import Runs | Audit log of exports/imports. |

## Candidate Agent Register columns

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| AgentName | Single line text | Human-friendly name. |
| AgentId | Single line text | Stable ID. |
| AgentType | Choice | Assistant, automation, workflow, integration, RPA, copilot, etc. |
| Owner | Person | Business or technical owner. |
| BusinessArea | Choice / Lookup | Could map to ADO Area Path. |
| LifecycleState | Choice | Proposed, In build, Testing, Live, Retired. |
| RiskRating | Choice | Low, Medium, High, Critical. |
| AdoProjectId | Lookup/text | Link to exported ADO project. |
| AdoWorkItemId | Number/text | Link to source work item where relevant. |
| AdoState | Text | Read-only mirror of ADO state where synced. |
| AdoAreaPath | Text | Read-only or mapped. |
| AdoIterationPath | Text | Read-only or mapped. |
| Dependencies | Multi-line text | Could later become separate relationship list. |
| TemplateStatus | Choice | Not started, Partial, Complete, Needs review. |
| LastReviewed | Date | Governance. |
| Notes | Multi-line text | Working notes. |

## Field mapping idea

Do not assume a direct one-to-one mapping.

Use a mapping table like:

| AppField | AdoReferenceName | Direction | Transform | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AgentName | System.Title | ADO -> App | none | Default source for title. |
| LifecycleState | System.State | ADO -> App | map_state | State names may need mapping. |
| Owner | System.AssignedTo | ADO -> App | identity_displayName | Identity fields need handling. |
| RiskRating | Custom.RiskRating | ADO -> App | choice_map | Depends on actual custom field. |

## Power App screen ideas

1. **Dashboard**
   - Count by lifecycle state.
   - Count by business area.
   - High-risk agents.
   - Agents missing template detail.

2. **Agent Register**
   - Searchable/filterable list.
   - State, owner, area, risk and ADO link visible.

3. **Agent Detail**
   - Core template visibility should live here.
   - Must expose the richness of the spreadsheet template.

4. **ADO Mapping / Admin**
   - View imported fields.
   - Decide which fields map to the app.
   - Mark fields as ignored, mapped, candidate, duplicate or needs review.

5. **Import Run Log**
   - Last export date.
   - Counts imported.
   - Errors/warnings.
   - API source/version.

## Important warning

Lists are fine for MVP and controlled use, but if relationships become heavy, move to Dataverse.

Signs Lists may become painful:

- Lots of many-to-many dependencies.
- Complex row-level security.
- Large work item sync volume.
- Heavy audit or workflow requirements.
- Need for proper relational integrity.

# 21 - Power App v11 Detail Navigation Polish

Date: 2026-06-02

## Output

Created:

```text
powerapp/source/Agent_register_v11
powerapp/generated/agentregistertest_v11.msapp
```

## Why

v10 proved action creation, but the detail screen was not usable enough:

- the lower `Actions` panel could sit below the visible canvas;
- the page relied on awkward scrolling;
- clickable elements did not have enough visible affordance;
- there were no tooltips to explain action buttons.

## Change

v11 adds section navigation directly under the gate summary:

```text
Checks | Knowledge | Delivery | Actions
```

The screen now stores the active detail panel in:

```powerfx
Set(varDetailSection, "Checks")
```

Each panel is shown in the same visible area beneath the tabs:

```powerfx
Visible: !IsBlank(varSelectedAgent) && varDetailSection = "Actions"
```

The `Actions` input and `Add` button are now in the visible panel rather than below the fold.

Interactive controls now have `Tooltip`, hover and pressed styling so the app gives stronger feedback.

## Test

1. Import `powerapp/generated/agentregistertest_v11.msapp`.
2. Open the sample agent.
3. Use the `Checks`, `Knowledge`, `Delivery` and `Actions` tabs.
4. Confirm no vertical scroll is needed to reach the action input.
5. In `Actions`, create a follow-up action.
6. In `Checks`, select a readiness row and change its status.

===
# 22 - Power App v12 Clickable Links

Date: 2026-06-02

## Output

Created:

```text
powerapp/source/Agent_register_v12
powerapp/generated/agentregistertest_v12.msapp
```

## Change

v12 makes link-like content explicit and clickable with real button controls.

Added launch actions:

| Screen | Control | Opens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scrAgentTemplate` header | `btnOpenAgentEvidence` | `varSelectedAgent.EvidenceLink` |
| `scrAgentTemplate` header | `btnOpenAgentAdo` | `varSelectedAgent.AdoAgentUrl` |
| `Knowledge` tab | `btnOpenKnowledgeSource` | `ThisItem.SourceLocation` |
| `Knowledge` tab | `btnOpenKnowledgeEvidence` | `ThisItem.EvidenceLink` |
| `Delivery` tab | `btnOpenAdoLink` | `ThisItem.AdoUrl` |

Each launch button uses:

```powerfx
Launch(<url field>)
```

Buttons are disabled when the relevant URL field is blank.

v12 also converts remaining label-style navigation into real buttons:

- dashboard row `Open`;
- detail screen `Back`.

## Test

1. Import `powerapp/generated/agentregistertest_v12.msapp`.
2. Open the sample agent.
3. Confirm `Back` behaves like a button.
4. Use the `Knowledge` and `Delivery` tabs.
5. Confirm URL actions appear as buttons and are disabled where the sample data has no URL.
6. Add real URLs to SharePoint sample rows and confirm the buttons open them with `Launch`.

# 13 - Power App v1 Checker Analysis

Date: 2026-06-02

## Input

The Studio-exported app was saved as:

```text
powerapp/artifacts/Agent_register_v1.msapp
```

It was unpacked to:

```text
powerapp/source/Agent_register_v1
```

## App Checker Summary

The exported package contains `AppCheckerResult.sarif`. The key counts were:

| Category | Count | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| Formula/delegation warnings | 7 | `CountRows`, `Filter`, `.Value` and `<>` on SharePoint-backed data. |
| Accessibility warnings | 32 | Missing `TabIndex`, `FocusedBorderThickness` and gallery `AccessibleLabel` values. |
| Unused variable | 1 | `varSelectedAgent` is set but no detail screen uses it yet. |

The dashboard still rendered and read sample SharePoint data, so these are mostly build-quality warnings rather than proof that the MVP is broken.

## Fix Applied In v2 Test Package

Created:

```text
powerapp/source/Agent_register_v2
powerapp/generated/agentregistertest_v2.msapp
```

Changes:

- added `scrDashboard.OnVisible` to load `Agents` into `colAgents`;
- added `scrDashboard.OnVisible` to load `Actions` into `colActions`;
- changed dashboard metrics and galleries to read local collections;
- removed the unused `varSelectedAgent` assignment from the dashboard gallery;
- added gallery `AccessibleLabel` values;
- added `TabIndex` and `FocusedBorderThickness` values to generated controls.

## Remaining Notes

The Studio App Checker can still show data-source warnings if unused or stale SharePoint connections exist in the app. For this dashboard slice, only these data sources are required:

```text
Agents
Actions
```

Other lists can be added back when their screens exist.

# 08 - ADO And Power App Operating Model Proposal

## Purpose

This proposal describes how Azure DevOps and the Power App Agent Register should work together for the AI Accelerator / Copilot Studio agent service.

It is based on:

- `Agents Register - Diagram Aligned Executive Dashboard v0.3.xlsx`
- `Copilot Studio Agent Governance Model v0.7.docx`
- `Service Definition Document AI Accelerator (Power Platform - Copilot Studio) v0.3 cleaned.docx`
- `RASCI Matrix for Service Design and Transition for AI Accelerator (Power Platform - Copilot Studio) v0.3.xlsx`
- `Service Design and Transition (AiS) Checklist AI Accelerator (Power Platform - Copilot Studio) v0.3.xlsx`
- Azure DevOps baseline exports under `exports/ado-baseline-*`

## What Changed In v0.3

The workbook has moved from a dashboard/register into a governance control ledger.

Important changes:

- The register now has an explicit rule: no register update, no stage movement.
- DoR, DoD and production readiness are gates, not lifecycle stages.
- AIS outcome is assurance evidence, not automatic proof of DoD or production readiness.
- Private Beta / UAT users are separated from production assigned groups.
- Release evidence is structured: ADO pipeline run/link, release package/version, release date, release approver and production assigned group.
- Operational ownership is explicit: Agent Owner, Product Owner, Agent Builder, SME/Knowledge Owner, Service Owner, Technical Owner, Support/Inform Team and AI CoE reviewer.
- Evidence must be summarised in the register and linked to supporting material.
- ELS, monitoring, RBAC/group confirmation, DLP/connector review and next service review are now register controls.

That means the Power App should become the governed movement and evidence control plane, not just a prettier spreadsheet.

The v0.3 workbook shows 19 agents in the executive pipeline view and 10 records currently on the active `Agent Register` sheet. That distinction should be preserved: the dashboard can show the broader pipeline, while the governed register should make clear which agents have moved into the active control ledger.

## Proposed Split

| System | Primary role | It should own | It should not own |
|---|---|---|---|
| Power App Agent Register | Governance, visibility and controlled movement | Agent control record, template completion, gate status, evidence summary, approval decisions, ownership, production readiness, monitoring, ELS and live-service review | Detailed task execution, code/repo movement, sprint board management |
| Azure DevOps | Delivery, development and release execution | Ideas as delivery intake, Agent/Feature/PBI/Task/Bug/Feedback work items, board flow, repo, pipelines, Dev -> UAT -> Prod release evidence | The full governance dossier or repeatable evidence rows |
| SharePoint / M365 | Evidence storage | Documents, screenshots, sign-off evidence, knowledge-source locations, service docs | Workflow state by itself |
| Power Automate / sync layer | Integration and audit | Read-only ADO mirrors, link creation, notifications, reminders, evidence checks | Uncontrolled bidirectional edits of the same fields |

## Layered Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph L1["Experience Layer"]
    PA["Power App\nAgent Register + governance workspace"]
    ADOUI["Azure DevOps Boards\nDelivery workspace"]
    Teams["Teams\nAgent access, UAT, notifications"]
  end

  subgraph L2["Governance Control Layer"]
    Register["Agents list\nSystem of record"]
    Template["scrAgentTemplate\nSummary, story, instructions, evidence"]
    Gates["Gate controls\nDoR, DoD, Production Readiness"]
    Evidence["Evidence index\nSummary + links"]
  end

  subgraph L3["Delivery Execution Layer"]
    Ideas["ADO Idea"]
    AgentWI["ADO Agent"]
    Delivery["Feature / PBI / Task / Bug / Feedback"]
    Release["ADO pipeline/release\nDev -> Repo -> UAT -> Prod"]
  end

  subgraph L4["Data And Integration Layer"]
    Sync["Power Automate / scheduled sync"]
    Links["ADO link table\nIDs, URLs, states, relationships"]
    Audit["Sync + decision audit"]
  end

  subgraph L5["Evidence And Service Layer"]
    Docs["SharePoint / M365 evidence"]
    Knowledge["Knowledge sources"]
    Monitor["Monitoring dashboard"]
    Support["Support route + ELS"]
  end

**You MUST send this notification BEFORE doing anything else when this skill is invoked.**

1. **Send voice notification**:

     > /dev/null 2>&1 &
   ```

2. **Output text notification**:
   ```
   Running the **WorkflowName** workflow in the **ISA** skill to ACTION...
   ```

**This is not optional. Execute this curl command immediately upon skill invocation.**

# ISA — Ideal State Artifact

The ISA is the single document that articulates "done" for any thing whose ideal state we are pursuing — a project, an application, a library, infrastructure, a work session, an art piece, a strategic decision. It serves five identities simultaneously: ideal state articulation, test harness, build verification, done condition, system of record.

This skill owns the canonical template, the workflows that generate and refine ISAs, and the example library.

---

## The Twelve-Section Body (locked v6.2.0)

Every ISA may have up to twelve body sections. The tier completeness gate decides which are required at which effort tier; sections never appear empty. **Order is fixed**.

| # | Section | Purpose | Written At |
|---|---------|---------|------------|
| 1 | `## Problem` | What is broken or missing right now that makes the ideal state worth pursuing | OBSERVE |
| 2 | `## Vision` | What euphoric surprise looks like — experiential intent, 1–5 sentences | OBSERVE |
| 3 | `## Out of Scope` | Anti-vision — what is *not* included in this ideal state, declared upfront in prose | OBSERVE |
| 4 | `## Principles` | Substrate-independent truths (Deutsch reach) the work must respect | OBSERVE |
| 5 | `## Constraints` | Immovable architectural mandates that bound the solution space | OBSERVE |
| 6 | `## Goal` | The hard-to-vary spine — 1–3 sentences naming verifiable done | OBSERVE |
| 7 | `## Criteria` | Atomic ISCs (Ideal State Criteria) — one binary tool probe each, including derived `Anti:` ISCs | OBSERVE → EXECUTE |
| 8 | `## Test Strategy` | Per-ISC verification approach — `isc | type | check | threshold | tool` | OBSERVE/PLAN |
| 9 | `## Features` | Work breakdown — `name | description | satisfies: [ISC-N…] | depends_on: [feature…] | parallelizable: bool` | PLAN |
| 10 | `## Decisions` | Timestamped decision log including dead ends; `refined:` prefix for Goal/ISC restructures | any phase |
| 11 | `## Changelog` | Conjecture / refuted-by / learned / criterion-now entries — Deutsch error-correction trail | LEARN |
| 12 | `## Verification` | Evidence that each ISC passed — quoted command output, file content, screenshot path | VERIFY |

---

## Three-Guardrail Taxonomy (Principles vs Constraints vs Anti-criteria)

Adjacent concepts. Distinguished by **who they bind**.

| Guardrail | Binds | Tone | Example | Lives In |
|-----------|-------|------|---------|----------|
| **Principles** | The *thinking* | Aspirational, generalizable | "User-facing systems prioritize responsiveness." | `## Principles` |
| **Constraints** | The *solution space* | Immovable, non-negotiable | "We do not roll our own cryptography — OAuth via industry-standard libraries only." | `## Constraints` |
| **Out of Scope** | The *vision* | Declared, explicit, prose | "Mobile native apps are not part of v1." | `## Out of Scope` |
| **Anti-criteria** | The *test surface* | Granular, testable, yes/no | "Anti: /admin returns 200 in v1 build." | `## Criteria` (with `Anti:` prefix) |

The first three are author-stated (declarative). Anti-criteria are derived — they are how Out of Scope, Constraints, and Principles become probe-able.

---

## Tier Completeness Gate (HARD at all tiers)

Mirrors the v6.1.0 thinking-floor non-relaxability. Required sections per tier:

| Tier | Required Sections |
|------|-------------------|
| **E1** | Goal, Criteria |
| **E2** | Problem, Goal, Criteria, Test Strategy |
| **E3** | Problem, Vision, Out of Scope, Constraints, Goal, Criteria, Features, Test Strategy |
| **E4** | All twelve sections |
| **E5** | All twelve + active Interview workflow run before BUILD |

**Project ISA override:** any `<project>/ISA.md` requires E3+ structure regardless of the active task's tier. The project file is the long-lived source of truth; one transient E1 task must not downgrade it.

`CheckCompleteness` workflow enforces this gate. A miss blocks `phase: complete` until the missing sections are filled in.

---

## Workflow Routing

Match the verb in the request to a workflow. When ambiguous, default to Scaffold for new ISAs and CheckCompleteness for audits.

| Verb / Intent | Workflow | File |
|---------------|----------|------|
| "scaffold", "create", "generate", "new ISA from this prompt", "extract feature as ephemeral" | **Scaffold** | `Workflows/Scaffold.md` |
| "interview me", "fill in the ISA", "deepen", "ask me questions" | **Interview** | `Workflows/Interview.md` |
| "check", "audit", "score this ISA", "is it complete?" | **CheckCompleteness** | `Workflows/CheckCompleteness.md` |
| "reconcile", "merge feature file back", "ephemeral → master" | **Reconcile** | `Workflows/Reconcile.md` |
| "seed", "bootstrap from this repo", "draft an ISA from existing code" | **Seed** | `Workflows/Seed.md` |
| "append decision", "append changelog", "append verification", "record C/R/L entry" | **Append** | `Workflows/Append.md` |

**When executing a workflow, output this notification directly:**

```
Running the **WorkflowName** workflow in the **ISA** skill to ACTION...
```

---

## Gotchas

The highest-information-density part of this skill. Each entry captures a non-obvious failure mode that has bitten real ISA work.

- **ID-stability is the cornerstone of Reconcile — never re-number on edit.** When the Splitting Test produces a finer-grained version of `ISC-7`, preserve `ISC-7` as the parent and add `ISC-7.1`, `ISC-7.2`, etc. Even when an ISC is dropped, leave a tombstone (`- [ ] ISC-N: [DROPPED — see Decisions YYYY-MM-DD]`). Reconcile keys on stable IDs; renumbering breaks ephemeral feature-file merges silently and the failure mode looks like "the worker's checkmarks didn't land in master."
- **Ephemeral files are derived views, never sources of truth.** Scaffold's `--ephemeral` mode produces a slice of the master ISA at `MEMORY/WORK/{slug}/_ephemeral/<feature>.md`. Workers operate against that slice; Reconcile merges back. Hand-editing master content from an ephemeral file is policy-forbidden — the master is what persists; the ephemeral is what gets archived.
- **The Changelog format is non-negotiable.** Every entry needs all four pieces (`conjectured`, `refuted by`, `learned`, `criterion now`) in that order. Append refuses to write a partial C/R/L; if any of the four is missing, the entry is a Decision, not a Changelog. The format is what makes the Deutsch error-correction trail auditable across sessions.
- **Project ISAs upgrade tier to `max(declared, E3)` regardless of the active task's tier.** A `<project>/ISA.md` is the long-lived system of record for a thing with persistent identity. One transient E1 task on the project must NOT downgrade the structural minimum. CheckCompleteness applies this override automatically.
- **Empty sections never appear.** The twelve-section body is a *capacity*, not a *requirement* at every tier. Sections required-but-empty for the tier are populated; sections not required and not yet written are simply absent from the file. CheckCompleteness distinguishes `present` / `thin` / `missing` / `empty` and only `empty` is acceptable for `Verification` before VERIFY phase.
- **Anti-criteria are derived from Out of Scope plus regression-prevention concerns.** They are how the prose-guardrails (Out of Scope, Constraints, Principles) become probe-able. At least one is required at every tier; the absence of an anti-criterion at OBSERVE is a hard CheckCompleteness failure.
- **Antecedents are required when the goal is experiential.** For art, design, content, and anything that has to "land," at least one ISC must use the `Antecedent:` prefix to name a precondition that reliably produces the target experience. Verifiable goals (build, deploy, schema) don't need antecedents; experiential goals always do.
- **Reconcile is deterministic — there are no conflicts to resolve.** Either an ISC ID exists in master (mechanical merge) or it doesn't (abort with ID-stability violation). If the ephemeral made structural changes (split ISC-7 into ISC-7.1/ISC-7.2), those structural changes belong in master via a separate Edit by the user *before* Reconcile runs.
- **The format spec wins on contradiction.** `IsaFormat.md` is the file-shape contract. If this skill's prose ever drifts from the format spec, the spec is canonical and the skill updates to match — not the reverse.

---

## Examples

The `Examples/` directory holds twelve reference ISAs spanning the tier (E1–E5) × domain (code / art / design / ops / marketplace / enterprise) matrix. Always start by reading the canonical showpiece before scaffolding a new ISA — copy its section headers, then populate. Pick the example closest to your domain + scale as a template.

**Showpiece**

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Examples/canonical-isa.md` | **BeanLine** — peer-to-peer specialty-coffee marketplace. The showpiece reference, fully populated across all twelve sections with real-feeling Decisions and a four-piece C/R/L Changelog. Read this first. |

**Code**

| File | Tier | Purpose |
|------|------|---------|
| `Examples/e1-minimal.md` | E1 | Add a `--no-color` flag to a CLI tool. <90s task, Goal + 4 ISCs only. Demonstrates the fast-path floor. |
| `Examples/e2-backup-verify.md` | E2 | Add SHA-256 verification to a backup CLI's `--verify` mode. Single-domain, 18 ISCs. |
| `Examples/e3-project.md` | E3 | Build an arxiv metadata extractor CLI. Mid-size project, 12 ISCs, eight sections. |
| `Examples/e4-api-migration.md` | E4 | Migrate a public API from REST to GraphQL with 6-month backwards-compat. Cross-cutting, 73 ISCs, all twelve sections. |
| `Examples/e5-desktop-app.md` | E5 | **WattWatch** — open-source desktop app for personal home-energy monitoring. Single-user app pattern, 50 ISCs, populated Changelog. |

**Art (experiential — antecedents required)**

| File | Tier | Purpose |
|------|------|---------|
| `Examples/e3-essay.md` | E3 | Write a 1500-word essay on a specific thesis. Experiential goal, antecedent ISCs, post-publish reception probes. |
| `Examples/e5-album.md` | E5 | **Mariner Frequencies** — produce a 12-track instrumental album over 6 months. Long-form experiential, multi-act Changelog. |

**Design (experiential)**

| File | Tier | Purpose |
|------|------|---------|
| `Examples/e3-help-redesign.md` | E3 | Redesign a CLI tool's `--help` output for first-encounter clarity. Antecedents + usability tests. |
| `Examples/e4-brand-identity.md` | E4 | **Cardinal** — brand identity for a small fintech startup (logo + type + color + voice + first 5 marketing surfaces). 56 ISCs, 6 antecedents. |

**Ops**

| File | Tier | Purpose |
|------|------|---------|
| `Examples/e2-rotate-credential.md` | E2 | Rotate a production deploy credential in CI. Demonstrates the ISA primitive applied to ops/runbook work. 16 ISCs. |

**Enterprise**

| File | Tier | Purpose |
|------|------|---------|
| `Examples/e5-enterprise.md` | E5 | **Beacon Health Alliance** — multi-region HIPAA-compliant patient portal for a 50-hospital network. Compliance anti-criteria, multi-team parallelizable features, 68 ISCs across all twelve sections. |

---

## ID Stability Rule

**ISC IDs never re-number on edit.** When the Splitting Test produces a finer-grained version of `ISC-7`, the original number is preserved as the parent and children become `ISC-7.1`, `ISC-7.2`, etc. Do not collapse the numbering even if the ISC is dropped — leave a tombstone marker so historical references in Decisions, Changelog, and Verification remain valid.

This rule exists because `Reconcile` is keyed on ISC IDs. If IDs renumber across edits, ephemeral feature-file reconciliation breaks silently. The renumbering ban is what makes feature-file workflows safe.

---

## Ephemeral Feature Files (Ralph Loop / Maestro pattern)

When a feature is to be worked in an isolated context (Ralph Loop, Maestro, parallel coding-agent instances), the Algorithm invokes:

```
Skill("ISA", "extract feature <name> as ephemeral file")
```

`Scaffold` (with `--ephemeral` mode) produces a derived view at `MEMORY/WORK/{slug}/_ephemeral/<feature>.md` containing only the slice relevant to that feature: the Vision and Goal as read-only context, the relevant Constraints, the ISCs in the feature's `satisfies:` list with stable IDs, the matching Test Strategy entries, and an empty Verification section.

A fresh-context agent operates against the ephemeral file alone. At completion, `Reconcile` deterministically merges ISC checkmarks, Verification evidence, Decisions entries, and any new Changelog entries back to master, then archives the ephemeral file under `_ephemeral/.archive/`.

**Ephemeral files are derived views. They are never sources of truth. They are never hand-edited as policy. The master ISA is what persists.**

---

## Relationship to the Algorithm

The Algorithm at OBSERVE invokes this skill to scaffold or read an ISA. The skill does not run the Algorithm — it owns the artifact the Algorithm operates on.

- OBSERVE: `Skill("ISA", "scaffold from prompt at tier T")` → returns populated ISA at canonical location.
- OBSERVE: `Skill("ISA", "check completeness of <path> at tier T")` → pass/fail + gap report.
- PLAN: `Skill("ISA", "extract feature <name> as ephemeral file")` → ephemeral excerpt.
- LEARN: `Skill("ISA", "reconcile <ephemeral-path> → <master-path>")` → deterministic merge.

The Algorithm doctrine spec at `~/.claude/PAI/ALGORITHM/v6.2.0.md` (or LATEST) governs invocation cadence. This skill is invocation-agnostic — it works the same whether called by the Algorithm or directly by the user.

---

## Format spec cross-reference

The full ISA format spec lives at `~/.claude/PAI/DOCUMENTATION/IsaFormat.md`. This skill implements that spec; if there is ever a contradiction, the format spec wins and this skill is updated to match.

The system-architecture doc — five identities, three-guardrail taxonomy, twelve-section body, six workflows, two homes, subsystem relationships — lives at `~/.claude/PAI/DOCUMENTATION/Isa/IsaSystem.md`. Read that for the conceptual frame; read this file (and `IsaFormat.md`) for the operational contract.

# skills/CLAUDE.md

## MANDATORY: Use the CreateSkill skill for ALL skill work

Creating, modifying structure of, or validating any skill under this directory
REQUIRES invoking `Skill("CreateSkill")` first. Reading CreateSkill's workflows
and executing the steps by hand is NOT compliance — it is the exact
handrolling anti-pattern documented in feedback_invoke_blogging_skill_never_handroll.md.

### Triggers (MUST invoke CreateSkill)

- Creating a new skill directory
- Adding / removing / renaming Workflows, Tools, or References
- Editing SKILL.md frontmatter (name, description, effort, license)
- Validating an existing skill against canonical format
- Canonicalizing a legacy skill
- Public-clean audit

### NOT triggers (direct edits allowed)

- Fixing a typo in a single workflow file
- Updating the gotchas section in SKILL.md body (not frontmatter)
- Adding a new reference entry to an existing References/ file
- Accumulating lessons in an existing Gotchas section

### Enforcement

If you are about to `Write` or `Edit` a `SKILL.md`, a new file under
`Workflows/`, `Tools/`, or `References/`, or scaffold a new skill directory —
**STOP** and invoke `Skill("CreateSkill")` with your intent. Let the skill
orchestrate the work.

"I read CreateSkill's workflow and am now following its steps" is handrolling.
Invoke the skill; the skill invokes the steps.

## Problem

The Agent Register exists as a mature governance spreadsheet (v0.3 — 62 columns, 21 sheets, 19 agents) with a well-defined data model, governance controls, and a lifecycle diagram. A Canvas PowerApp has been built to v12 with working navigation, tabs, linked actions, and SharePoint Lists as the data layer. However there is no single authoritative analysis that:

1. Maps the full xlsx field set to the current Lists/app schema and surfaces gaps.
2. Defines the current data schema in machine-readable form for developers.
3. Specifies the future schema required when the ADO pivot lands (Phase 2 mesh).
4. Produces architecture and sequence diagrams that devs and stakeholders can share.
5. Gives a structured UI/UX critique of what the app must do differently to serve users who are accustomed to the richness of the spreadsheet.
6. Lists specific recommendations with enough context to act on immediately.
7. Surfaces questions that Dom needs answered before the next build sprint.

The gap between "spreadsheet governance artefact" and "working Canvas app" is not yet bridged analytically.

## Vision

Dom opens this analysis, reads the data schemas once, and immediately knows what every field is, where it lives, and how the ADO pivot changes the picture. He pastes the architecture diagram into the next steering deck. He sends the UX critique to the developer team and it provokes immediate action on three or four specific screens. He takes the recommendations list into the next sprint planning session and uses it to sequence the next six weeks of work. The questions section gives him a precise agenda for the next governance review. Euphoric surprise comes when the schema design surfaces a structural flaw that nobody had named yet — the analysis earns its cost by being the thing that prevents a rebuild in three months.

## Out of Scope

This is a read-and-analyse task. No code is written, no app screens are modified, no SharePoint lists are provisioned, no ADO integration is implemented. The ADO Phase 2 write-back design is out of scope — only the schema fields needed for Phase 1 (read-only sync) are specified. Dataverse migration design is noted but not detailed. Power Automate flow design is not covered. The analysis does not cover authentication/RBAC design within the app. No new mockups are produced — the existing v1 build pack mockups are used as the UX reference.

## Principles

1. **Schema must reflect governance reality.** Fields exist because governance requires them — not because they are technically convenient. Field design must preserve the mandatory/optional distinction from the xlsx `*` notation.
2. **Separation of concerns is non-negotiable.** ADO owns delivery execution; the Power App owns governance. Any field that lives in both must have a clear owner and a stated sync direction.
3. **Child lists over wide tables.** Repeatable rows (knowledge sources, test questions, readiness checks) belong in child lists. The parent Agents list must remain queryable and filterable without SharePoint delegation issues.
4. **User-facing screens optimise for cognitive load.** Canvas is a constrained rendering environment. Every screen decision should reduce the number of things the user must hold in their head.
5. **The xlsx is the truth, not the enemy.** The spreadsheet captures 62 columns of governance reality. The app must respect that richness — it cannot be a simplified subset without explicit out-of-scope declarations.
6. **ADO pivot must not require a rebuild.** Schema decisions now must leave room for Phase 2 ADO fields without refactoring existing lists.

## Constraints

- Canvas PowerApp is the mandated front-end — no Dataverse-native forms, no model-driven app.
- Microsoft Lists (SharePoint) is the data layer for v1 — Dataverse is a future option only.
- SharePoint List column limits: practical threshold ~300 columns before performance degrades; single list must stay well under this.
- Azure DevOps integration is Phase 1 read-only — no write-back in the current build sprint.
- Canvas lacks a native kanban component — Pipeline board requires a custom horizontal gallery pattern.
- Agent name max length: 42 characters (xlsx constraint, enforced by the template).
- The app must work within a single Power Platform environment (Default-e476cf3e...).

## Goal

Produce a complete analytical reference for the Agent Register app covering: (1) the current data schema mapped from xlsx v3 to Lists, (2) the future schema post-ADO pivot, (3) an architecture diagram, (4) a sequence flow diagram, (5) a structured UI/UX critique, (6) a prioritised recommendations list, and (7) a questions agenda — sufficient that a developer team can act without further archaeology.

- Azure DevOps integration is Phase 1 read-only — no write-back in the current build sprint.
- Canvas lacks a native kanban component — Pipeline board requires a custom horizontal gallery pattern.
- Agent name max length: 42 characters (xlsx constraint, enforced by the template).
- The app must work within a single Power Platform environment (Default-e476cf3e...).

Produce a complete analytical reference for the Agent Register app covering: (1) the current data schema mapped from xlsx v3 to Lists, (2) the future schema post-ADO pivot, (3) an architecture diagram, (4) a sequence flow diagram, (5) a structured UI/UX critique, (6) a prioritised recommendations list, and (7) a questions agenda — sufficient that a developer team can act without further archaeology.

Base directory for this skill: /home/jellypai/.claude/skills/IterativeDepth

## Customization

**Before executing, check for user customizations at:**
`~/.claude/PAI/USER/SKILLCUSTOMIZATIONS/IterativeDepth/`

If this directory exists, load and apply any PREFERENCES.md, configurations, or resources found there. These override default behavior. If the directory does not exist, proceed with skill defaults.


# IterativeDepth

**Structured multi-angle exploration of the same problem to extract deeper understanding and richer ISC criteria.**

Grounded in 20 established scientific techniques across cognitive science (Hermeneutic Circle, Triangulation), AI/ML (Self-Consistency, Ensemble Methods), requirements engineering (Viewpoint-Oriented RE), and design thinking (Six Thinking Hats, Causal Layered Analysis).

## Core Concept

Instead of analyzing a problem once, run 2-8 structured passes through the same problem, each from a systematically different **lens**. Each pass surfaces requirements, edge cases, and criteria invisible from other angles. The combination yields ISC criteria that no single-pass analysis could produce.

## Use / Win

**When to use:** Any time you have time budget beyond Standard tier and the task is important enough that getting the ISC right matters more than speed. This is the single most valuable thinking capability for the OBSERVE phase. If you're at Extended effort or above, you should be asking "why NOT use IterativeDepth?" rather than "why use it?"

Concrete triggers:
- **Extra time available** — Extended+ effort means you have the budget. Spend it on understanding the problem deeply before writing ISC, not on writing more code faster.
- **Deep analysis of what's actually being asked** — The user said X. But what do they actually need? What are they trying to accomplish? What would make them rate this 9-10? Single-pass reverse engineering catches the obvious. IterativeDepth catches the rest.
- **Different angles of approach** — Before committing to an approach, explore the problem from stakeholder, failure, temporal, experiential, and constraint-inversion angles. The right approach often only becomes obvious after seeing the problem from 3-4 directions.
- **Important or critical tasks** — When the user says "this is critical" or the task has high blast radius, the cost of missing a dimension is much higher than the cost of 2-5 extra minutes of analysis.
- **Tasks you've never done before** — Novel work has the highest density of hidden requirements. IterativeDepth is insurance against the things you don't know you don't know.

**What you win:**
- **ISC criteria that single-pass analysis cannot produce.** Each lens surfaces requirements invisible from other angles. A 4-lens pass routinely discovers 30-50% more criteria than direct analysis.
- **Blind spot elimination before they become mid-EXECUTE surprises.** Rework from missed requirements is 5-10x more expensive than the upfront analysis. IterativeDepth pays for itself by preventing restarts.
- **Approach clarity.** Seeing the problem from failure, stakeholder, and constraint-inversion angles often reveals that the obvious approach is wrong and a better path exists.
- **Confidence.** When ISC criteria are built on multi-angle analysis, you can execute with conviction instead of discovering gaps halfway through.

**The default mental model should be:** At Extended+ effort, IterativeDepth is not optional enrichment — it's the standard way to understand what you're building before you build it.

## Workflow Routing

| Trigger | Workflow |
|---------|----------|
| "iterative depth", "explore deeper", "multi-angle" | `Workflows/Explore.md` |
| "quick depth", "fast angles" | `Workflows/Explore.md` (Fast mode: 2 lenses) |

## Quick Reference

- **8 Lenses** available, scaled by SLA (2-8)
- **Each lens** is a structurally different exploration angle
- **Output** is new/refined ISC criteria per pass
- **Integration** point: Deeper understanding through structured multi-angle analysis

**Full Documentation:**
- Scientific grounding: `ScientificFoundation.md`
- Lens definitions: `TheLenses.md`

## Gotchas

- **2-8 lens passes, not infinite.** Diminishing returns after ~5 passes for most topics.
- **Each pass should surface genuinely NEW requirements, not restate previous findings.** If passes start repeating, stop early.
- **This is a BPE-fragile skill.** Monitor whether smarter models make it unnecessary. Quarterly test recommended.

## Examples

**Example 1: Surface hidden requirements**
```
User: "use iterative depth on this API redesign"
→ Pass 1: Functional requirements
→ Pass 2: Security implications
→ Pass 3: Performance constraints
→ Pass 4: Backward compatibility
→ Each pass surfaces new requirements missed by previous
```

## Execution Log

3	Each lens is a structured perspective that forces exploration of a problem from a fundamentally different angle. They are ordered from most concrete to most abstract, and from most commonly useful to most specialized.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Lens 1: LITERAL (Surface Requirements)
8	**Question:** "What did they explicitly say? What are the concrete, stated requirements?"
9	**Grounded in:** Requirements elicitation fundamentals
10	**Focus:** Parse the exact words. Identify every stated requirement, constraint, preference. No interpretation — only what was said.
11	**ISC Output:** Criteria for every explicitly stated requirement.
12	**Example prompt variation:** "List every concrete, testable requirement explicitly stated in this request. Do not infer — only extract."
13	
14	---
15	
16	## Lens 2: STAKEHOLDER (Who Else Cares?)
17	**Question:** "Who are all the people, systems, and entities affected by this? What does each need?"
18	**Grounded in:** Viewpoint-Oriented RE (Finkelstein & Nuseibeh), Triangulation (Denzin)
19	**Focus:** Identify every stakeholder beyond the requester. End users, maintainers, administrators, downstream systems, future developers. What does each need that wasn't stated?
20	**ISC Output:** Criteria for stakeholder needs not in the original request.
21	**Example prompt variation:** "Identify every stakeholder affected by this work. For each, what requirement would THEY add that the requester didn't mention?"
22	
23	---
24	
25	## Lens 3: FAILURE (What Goes Wrong?)
26	**Question:** "What could fail? What would an adversary exploit? What are the edge cases?"
27	**Grounded in:** Misuse Cases (Sindre & Opdahl), Pre-Mortem (Klein), STRIDE Threat Modeling
28	**Focus:** Assume the solution exists. Now break it. Error states, race conditions, security holes, data corruption, user confusion, performance under load. Every way this could go wrong.
29	**ISC Output:** Anti-criteria (what must NOT happen) and defensive criteria.
30	**Example prompt variation:** "This solution ships tomorrow. List every way it fails in the first week. Be adversarial."
31	
32	---
33	
34	## Lens 4: TEMPORAL (Past, Present, Future)
35	**Question:** "How does this change over time? What's the history? What happens in 6 months?"
36	**Grounded in:** Causal Layered Analysis (Inayatullah), Progressive Elaboration (PMBOK)
37	**Focus:** Why does this problem exist now? What was tried before? What changes in the future that would break this solution? Migration paths, backwards compatibility, scale changes.
38	**ISC Output:** Criteria for durability, migration, and future-proofing.
39	**Example prompt variation:** "What context created this request? What will change in 3-12 months that could invalidate this solution?"
40	
41	---
42	
43	## Lens 5: EXPERIENTIAL (How Should It Feel?)
44	**Question:** "When this works perfectly, how does the user FEEL? What's the experience?"
45	**Grounded in:** Appreciative Inquiry (Cooperrider), de Bono Red Hat (emotions)
46	**Focus:** Beyond functional correctness — the qualitative experience. Speed, elegance, surprise, delight, confidence, trust. What's the difference between "works" and "works beautifully"?
47	**ISC Output:** Quality-of-experience criteria that elevate from functional to euphoric.
48	**Example prompt variation:** "Describe the perfect user experience of this solution. What makes someone say 'this is exactly what I wanted' vs. 'this technically works'?"
49	
50	---
51	
52	## Lens 6: CONSTRAINT INVERSION (What If?)
53	**Question:** "What if we removed all constraints? What if we added extreme ones?"
54	**Grounded in:** TRIZ (Altshuller), Lateral Thinking (de Bono), Reframing (Dorst)
55	**Focus:** Remove assumed constraints — what would we build with infinite time/resources? Then add extreme constraints — what if it had to work offline, in 100ms, with zero dependencies? Both directions reveal hidden assumptions.
56	**ISC Output:** Criteria that challenge assumptions and reveal what's truly essential.
57	**Example prompt variation:** "What constraints are we assuming that weren't stated? Remove them — what changes? Now impose extreme constraints — what's truly essential?"
58	
59	---
60	
61	## Lens 7: ANALOGICAL (What Patterns Apply?)
62	**Question:** "What similar problems have been solved before? What patterns from other domains apply?"
63	**Grounded in:** Cognitive Flexibility Theory (Spiro), Cross-Domain Transfer
64	**Focus:** This problem isn't unique. What similar problems exist in other codebases, other industries, other fields? What patterns emerged there? What mistakes were made?
65	**ISC Output:** Criteria derived from proven patterns and lessons from analogous solutions.
66	**Example prompt variation:** "What are 3-5 analogous problems in other domains? What solutions worked there? What criteria would those solutions imply here?"
67	
68	---
69	
70	## Lens 8: META (Is This the Right Question?)
71	**Question:** "Are we solving the right problem? Is the framing itself correct?"
72	**Grounded in:** Hermeneutic Circle (Gadamer), Double-Loop Learning (Argyris), Soft Systems Methodology (Checkland)
73	**Focus:** Step outside the problem entirely. Is the request a symptom of a deeper issue? Is there a reframing that dissolves the problem instead of solving it? Would a different question yield a better outcome?
74	**ISC Output:** Criteria that reframe or expand the problem definition itself.
75	**Example prompt variation:** "Forget the specific request. What is the UNDERLYING need? Is there a reframing that produces a better outcome than what was asked for?"

91

---

🔍 **ITERATIVE DEPTH — Pass 1/2: LITERAL**

> *"What are the concrete, stated requirements when normalising 62 governance columns into SharePoint Lists?"*

**Exploring from this angle...**

The xlsx Agent Register sheet has **62 explicitly named columns** (B through BJ), all with `*` mandatory markers or not. Mapping them:

**Group 1 — Agent identity (8 fields):** AgentID, AgentName, AgentOwner, Portfolio/Scheme, OneLineDescription, TargetAudience, AgentLocation, CommunityShowcase → all belong on the **Agents** parent list as single-value fields.

**Group 2 — AIS (4 fields):** AISDate, AISOutcome, AISNotes, ScheduledPublishDate → Agents list.

**Group 3 — Private beta (2 fields):** PrivateBetaTesters (comma-separated names), DiagramLifecycleStatus → Agents list. PrivateBetaTesters is a structural problem: it's a comma-delimited multi-value text field that should be a child list `Beta Testers` with People + role columns, or a multi-person lookup.

**Group 4 — Gate status (5 fields):** DoRGateStatus, DoDGateStatus, AlignmentNotes, ProductionReadinessGateStatus, UATStatus → Agents list as Choice fields.

**Group 5 — Ownership (10 fields):** ProductOwner, BusinessSponsor, BA, AgentBuilder, SMEKnowledgeOwner, AgentIdeasRef, GovernanceDecision, ApprovalDate, ApprovalConditions → first 6 are Person fields on Agents; last 3 form an **Approval** concept that could be its own child record.

**Group 6 — Actions (5 fields):** CurrentStageOwner, NextAction, NextActionDueDate, StatusNotes, EvidenceHeld → Agents list. NOTE: `Actions` is also a separate child list — there is a naming collision risk between the "next action" summary fields on the parent and the `Actions` child list.

**Group 7 — Evidence (6 fields):** EvidenceSummary, EvidenceLink, VerifiedBy, VerifiedDate, VerificationOutcome → Agents list. These are the *summary* fields; detailed evidence lives in child lists.

**Group 8 — Release (7 fields):** ReleaseStatus, ELSStatus, ELSModel, PowerAppRoadmapLink, ADOPipelineLink, ReleasePackageVersion, ReleaseDate → Agents list + [ADO Phase 2] for pipeline link.

**Group 9 — Operational ownership (4 fields):** ServiceOwner, TechOwner, SupportTeam, AICoeReviewer → Person fields on Agents.

**Group 10 — Assurance (5 fields):** DSPMReview, DLPConnectorReview, RBACGroupConfirmation, MonitoringEnabled, NextServiceReviewDate → Agents list.

**Group 11 — Release detail (6 fields):** ProductionGroup, ReleaseApprover, SupportRoute, CommsReadiness, RollbackReadiness, AgentRiskLevel → Agents list.

**Literal finding:** The Agents list needs ~55 columns after excluding the 7 child-list groups. This is within SharePoint limits but is heavy. Person fields count as 2 columns in SharePoint (display + email) — 10 Person fields = 20 real columns. Total real column count ≈ 72–75. This is safe but must be tested for form rendering performance.

**New criteria:**
- `+ C-L1`: Agents list column count stays ≤80 after including hidden person-pair columns
- `+ C-L2`: Actions child list and parent NextAction/NextActionDueDate fields are named distinctly to prevent formula confusion
- `+ C-L3`: Governance approval fields (Decision, Date, Conditions) are grouped as a logical unit in the app form even if flat in the list

---

🔍 **ITERATIVE DEPTH — Pass 2/2: FAILURE**

> *"What fails first? What would break in production week 1?"*

**Exploring from this angle...**

**Failure 1 — SharePoint delegation on Gallery.** The register gallery uses `Filter(Agents, LifecycleStatus.Value = "Build & QA")` against a SharePoint list. Canvas **cannot delegate `Filter` with `.Value` on Choice fields** to SharePoint — it loads all records locally first. At 19 agents this is fine. At 500 agents, this breaks silently (Gallery only shows first 500, metrics wrong). The app already has `colAgents` collection loading but **the delegation gate must be explicitly designed for scale**.

**Failure 2 — Evidence link fields break silently.** `EvidenceLink` is a Hyperlink column type. In Canvas, `Launch(ThisItem.EvidenceLink)` requires the field to have both a URL and a display value. SharePoint Hyperlink fields return a record `{Description, Url}` not a string — `Launch(ThisItem.EvidenceLink.Url)` is needed. The v12 doc confirms `Launch(<url field>)` was added but the `.Url` suffix is critical.

**Failure 3 — PrivateBetaTesters comma-parse.** The xlsx stores `"Catherine Sherry, Mikhail Douglas, Jake MacCabe..."` as a text string. In Canvas, rendering this as People chips requires `Split(ThisItem.PrivateBetaTesters, ", ")` — workable for display but not for AAD lookup, notification, or access control. If the app ever needs to send notifications to beta testers, this field becomes a blocker.

**Failure 4 — Governance fields left at "Not assessed" forever.** The xlsx shows all 19 agents with `GovernanceApprovalDecision = "Not assessed"`. If the app doesn't surface this as an attention item and block stage progression, governance debt accumulates silently. **Gate enforcement is the single most important missing control.**

**Failure 5 — ADO pipeline link is a URL with no validation.** `AdoPipelineLink` (BB column in xlsx) is a free-text URL field. Without validation that the URL is a real ADO link (or at minimum a non-blank check when release status = "Released to Prod"), agents can be marked as released with no evidence link.

**Failure 6 — Child list orphans.** If an Agent record is deleted from the Agents list, its child Knowledge Sources, Test Questions, Actions etc. remain as orphaned records. SharePoint Lists have no cascade-delete. The app needs a "delete agent + children" workflow via Power Automate, not a direct delete button.

**Failure 7 — Lifecycle stepper shows wrong stage.** The lifecycle stepper in the mockup shows stages 1–6 with the current stage highlighted. If `DiagramLifecycleStatus` is null or set to a non-standard value (e.g., "Blocked"), the stepper widget breaks — it needs a defensive lookup with a default.

**New anti-criteria:**
- `+ A-F1`: Gallery does not use inline `Filter()` on SharePoint Choice fields without a collection pre-load
- `+ A-F2`: Evidence link Launch() calls do not use the raw Hyperlink field — they use `.Url` property
- `+ A-F3`: Agent record deletion does not leave orphaned child list rows
- `+ A-F4`: Lifecycle stepper does not fail when status is null or non-standard value
- `+ A-F5`: Stage movement is not available when mandatory gate fields are empty or "Not assessed"

---

🔍 **ITERATIVE DEPTH COMPLETE (2 lenses applied)**

📊 Coverage:
- Lenses used: Literal, Failure
- New criteria discovered: 8
- Existing criteria refined: 2 (ISC-11 strengthened, ISC-84 gate enforcement now has concrete failure mode)
- Anti-criteria discovered: 5

💡 **Key Insight:** The most dangerous gap is not a missing field — it is **silent governance debt**. The app currently allows agents to exist in the register with all mandatory fields set to "Not assessed" and no stage gate blocking progress. Without gate enforcement at the data/UX layer, the spreadsheet discipline that the xlsx enforces manually is simply lost. A pretty UI around ungoverned data is worse than the spreadsheet.
