Now the full analysis document:

════ PAI | NATIVE MODE ═══════════════════════
🗒️ TASK: Agent Register full analysis — schema, UX, recommendations

---

## Current Data Schema: xlsx → SharePoint Lists Mapping

### Core: Agents List (62 columns → 1 primary list, 40 fields)

| Field Group | xlsx Columns | SP Field | Type | Mandatory |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Identity** | Agent Name, Summary, URL | AgentName, AgentSummary, AgentUrl | Single line / Multi-line | Yes |
| **Ownership** | Owner, Department, Portfolio | Owner, Department, Portfolio | Person / Choice / Lookup | Yes |
| **Lifecycle** | Stage, ADO State | LifecycleStage, ADODeliveryState | Choice | Yes |
| **User Story** | As a / I want to / So that | UserStoryAsA, UserStantTo, SoThat | Multi-line | Yes |
| **Business case** | Problem solved, Target audience | BusinessProblem, TargetAudience | Multi-line | Yes |
| **Instructions** | Agent instructions | AgentInstructions | Multi-line | Yes |
| **Topic titles** | Topic titles | AgentTopics | Multi-line | No |
| **Risk flags** | Contains PII, Web search, Uses tools, Uses triggers | ContainsPII, WebSearchEnabled, UsesTools, UsesTriggers | Yes/No | Yes |
| **PII notes** | PII notes | PIINotes | Multi-line | Conditional |
| **Model** | Model used | ModelUsed | Choice | No |
| **Evaluation** | Evaluator, Date, Outcome, Notes, Feasibility score | EvaluatorName, EvaluationDate, EvaluationOutcome, EvaluationNotes, FeasibilityScore | Person / Date / Choice / Multi-line / Number | No |
| **AIS** | AIS reviewer, date, outcome, notes | AISReviewer, AISReviewDate, AISOutcome, AISNotes | Person / Date / Choice / Multi-line | No |
| **DoR gate** | DoR status, date, approver | DORStatus, DORDate, DORApprover | Choice / Date / Person | No |
| **DoD gate** | DoD status, date, approver | DODStatus, DODDate, DODApprover | Choice / Date / Person | No |
| **Prod gate** | ProdReady status, date, approver | ProdReadyStatus, ProdReadyDate, ProdReadyApprover | Choice / Date / Person | No |
| **Deployment** | Dev URL, UAT URL, Prod URL, Solution name, First deployed, Last reviewed | StudioUrlDev, StudioUrlUAT, StudioUrlProd, SolutionName, DateFirstDeployed, DateLastReviewed | Hyperlink / Single line / Date | No |
| **Template completeness** | Completion % | TemplateCompletionPct | Number (calculated) | Auto |

### Child Lists (7 — linked to Agents via Lookup)

| List | Key Columns | Rows per agent |
|---|---|---|
| KnowledgeSources | SourceName, Type, URL, Quality, Sensitivity, LoginRequired, AgentAccess, UserAccess | 1–10 |
| TestQuestions | Question, ExpectedBehaviour, PassFail, TestedBy, TestDate | 5–20 |
| ReadinessChecks | CheckItem, Category (DoR/DoD/Prod), Status, EvidenceUrl, Notes | 15–30 |
| Actions | ActionTitle, ActionType, ActionUrl, Description | 1–10 |
| PromotionDecisions | Stage, Decision, DecidedBy, DecisionDate, Notes | 1 per gate |
| Reviews | ReviewType, Reviewer, Date, Outcome, Notes | 1–5 |
| ADOLinks | ADOWorkItemId, WorkItemType, Title, State, URL | 1–5 |

### Reference Lists (5 — controlled vocabularies)

| List | Values |
|---|---|
| Portfolios | Shared Reg, LCAD, … |
| RiskCategories | PII, External data, Tool use, … |
| LifecycleStages | Intake, Evaluate, Approve, Design, Build&QA, UAT, ELS, Live, Retired |
| Environments | Dev, UAT, Prod |
| Personas | Staff, Manager, Citizen, External |

---

## Future Schema: ADO Pivot (Phase 1 — Read-only Sync)

13 new fields on **Agents List** (Power Automate writes, users read-only):

| Field | Type | Source |
|---|---|---|
| ADOWorkItemId | Number | ADO Agent work item ID |
| ADOWorkItemUrl | Hyperlink | Direct link to ADO item |
| ADODeliveryState | Choice | Agent WIT state (New/In Progress/Testing/…) |
| ADOIterationPath | Single line | Sprint/iteration |
| ADOAreaPath | Single line | Team area |
| ADOAssignedTo | Single line | ADO assigned engineer |
| ADOLastSyncedAt | Date/Time | When PA last updated these fields |
| ADOBuildBranch | Single line | Linked repo branch |
| ADOSolutionExportUrl | Hyperlink | Solution export artifact |
| ADOEnvironmentsDeploy | Multi-line | Dev/UAT/Prod deploy status JSON blob |
| ADOReleasePipelineUrl | Hyperlink | Release pipeline link |
| ADOOpenBugCount | Number | Open bugs from ADO |
| ADOLastReleaseDate | Date/Time | Most recent successful release |

**Phase 2 additions** (write-back — future): ADOCreateWorkItem (Yes/No toggle), ADOPromotionTrigger (Text), ADOSyncErrors (Multi-line).

---

## UI/UX Review

### Critical Issues

**C1 — Gallery delegation breaks at scale**
`Filter(AgentsList, LifecycleStage.Value = selectedStage)` is not delegable. With 19 agents it works; at 500 it silently caps at the delegation limit (500 by default, configurable to 2000). The board and register views will silently show partial data with zero warning to users.
*Fix:* Pre-load all agents into a collection at OnStart with `ClearCollect(colAgents, AgentsList)` — 19 agents is safe, stays safe to ~2,000. Filter the collection, not the list.

**C2 — Gate enforcement is advisory only**
The DoR, DoD, and Production Readiness gates are UI affordances but the underlying SharePoint record has no enforced constraint. A user can set `LifecycleStage = "UAT"` directly without a DoR or DoD approval on record. All 19 current agents show `GovernanceApprovalDecision = "Not assessed"` — the gates have never been exercised.
*Fix:* Gate transition buttons should be the only route to stage change — disable the direct `LifecycleStage` field on the form. Gate approval records must exist and be marked "Approved" before the transition button activates.

**C3 — PrivateBetaTesters is a free-text field**
The UAT tester list is stored as a comma-delimited string. Can't query individual testers, can't send targeted notifications, can't track per-tester completion. Reported in ISA.
*Fix:* Move to TestQuestions child list with a `TestedBy` Person column, or add a UATTesters child list.

**C4 — Kanban board has no Power Apps native equivalent**
The `04_pipeline_board.png` mockup shows a multi-column drag-and-drop Kanban. Canvas apps have no native Kanban component — this requires a gallery-per-column layout with `Patch()` on drag. Horizontal scrolling in Canvas at tablet viewport is brittle.
*Fix:* Use a horizontally-arranged `Gallery per stage` (fixed columns, no drag). Or pivot to a `Pipeline Board` screen that uses the same filtered gallery list as the register, grouped by stage. Reserve the Kanban metaphor for a future model-driven layer.

**C5 — Template completion percentage is calculated in the app, not stored**
If completeness logic changes, historical snapshots become inconsistent. At 62 fields with conditional mandatory rules, the formula is already fragile.
*Fix:* Calculate and write `TemplateCompletionPct` to the list on each save via `Patch()`. Store, don't always derive.

**C6 — No breadcrumb or deep-link navigation**
From the detail screen, "Back" returns to the register list but loses any applied filter. There is no direct URL to an individual agent record (Canvas doesn't support deep links to records natively without embedding parameters).
*Fix:* Persist filter state in a global variable (`gvSelectedStage`, `gvSelectedPortfolio`) and restore on Back navigation. For deep links, consider using the `Param()` function with an embedded app URL that accepts `agentId` as a query parameter.

**C7 — No offline or low-connectivity indicator**
If SharePoint is unreachable, collections fail silently. On a large template save with `Patch()` on multiple child lists, partial failure leaves data in an inconsistent state.
*Fix:* Wrap multi-list Patch operations in `IfError()` with a rollback notification. Display a connectivity banner via a `Timer` check on OnStart.

### Positive Findings

- **Tab-based detail navigation** (v11: Summary/Gate Review/Knowledge/Delivery/Actions) is solid — mirrors natural workflow, avoids information overload on a single screen.
- **Lifecycle stepper component** gives executives instant visual orientation — worth protecting.
- **Intake wizard (5 steps)** is a genuine UX win; staged disclosure prevents form abandonment.
- **Template completeness indicator (78%)** gives developers a clear progress signal — high value if data is trustworthy (see C5).
- **Mockup visual design** (stage badges, color-coded lifecycle bar) is polished for a Canvas app — sets good expectations with stakeholders.

---

## Recommendations

| ID | Recommendation | Priority | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | **Enforce gate transitions** — disable direct LifecycleStage field; gate buttons are the only promotion path | High | M |
| R2 | **Pre-load Agents into collection** (ClearCollect on OnStart) — fixes delegation, enables filter/sort everywhere | High | S |
| R3 | **Store TemplateCompletionPct on Patch** — write the calculated value back, don't re-derive on every screen | High | S |
| R4 | **Replace PrivateBetaTesters free-text with UATTesters child list** — enables per-tester notifications and completion tracking | High | M |
| R5 | **Replace Kanban drag-drop mockup with Gallery-per-stage board** — achievable in Canvas, no unsupported components | Medium | M |
| R6 | **Persist filter state across navigation** (global vars) + add Back-button state restoration | Medium | S |
| R7 | **Build Power Automate Phase 1 ADO sync first** — even read-only delivery state on each agent record closes the biggest visibility gap | Medium | L |
| R8 | **Add governance health dashboard widget** — count of agents with no gate approvals on record, flag as "governance debt" | Medium | M |
| R9 | **Add IfError wrapping on all multi-list Patch operations** — silent partial saves are worse than visible errors | Low | S |

---

## Questions

| ID | Question | For |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 | The DoR/DoD/Production Readiness gate approvals are not currently enforced. Is this intentional (trust users) or is enforcement needed before pilot? | Product Owner |
| Q2 | Are all 19 agents in the register expected to go back through the governance process, or is the gate enforcement for new agents only? | Programme Lead |
| Q3 | Phase 1 ADO sync is read-only. What is the trigger to start this build — is it gated on the PowerApp reaching a stable state? | Dev Lead |
| Q4 | The AIS Review section exists in the app. Who owns the AIS review process and what evidence is required before sign-off? | Compliance / AIS team |
| Q5 | ELS periods are defined (5/10/20 days) but there is no ELS-end automation. Is manual promotion from ELS to Live acceptable or does this need a scheduled flow? | Operations |
| Q6 | The xlsx tracks 19 agents. How many agents are expected in 12 months — this directly affects the delegation risk decision in R2 | Product Owner |
| Q7 | The Kanban board is in the mockups. Is it a must-have for v1 or a nice-to-have? (It's the hardest screen to build correctly in Canvas) | Stakeholders |
| Q8 | Knowledge sources have a `Sensitivity` field and a `LoginRequired` flag. Who validates these before the agent goes to UAT — is that part of AIS review? | AIS Reviewer |
| Q9 | The xlsx has a `Submitted By` field separate from `Owner`. Are these always the same person or does the app need to show submitter lineage separately? | UX / Data |

---

## Structural Issues

1. **62-column flat sheet is not a data model** — it is a spreadsheet that grew. The 7 child-data groups (knowledge, tests, checklist, actions, decisions, reviews, ADO links) are repeating-row data masquerading as columns. Normalisation into child lists is non-optional for a production app.

2. **Governance state and delivery state are conflated** — `LifecycleStage` in the spreadsheet tracks both build progress and production maturity (Introduction/Growth/Maturity/Decline). These are two orthogonal dimensions. The app needs two separate indicators: **Delivery Stage** (Intake→Live) and **Adoption Maturity** (New→Decline).

3. **No single source of truth for stage** — stage is currently in both the PowerApp list and ADO work item state. Without Phase 1 sync, they will diverge. Before ADO sync, the PowerApp is the SoT; after Phase 1, ADO delivery state becomes the primary signal for build progress while PowerApp owns governance stage.

4. **Silent governance debt** — all 19 agents have `GovernanceApprovalDecision = "Not assessed"`. The app shows them without any flag. An executive reading the dashboard currently has no signal that none of these agents have been formally approved to be in production. This is the most urgent governance risk.

5. **Evidence fields are free text** — the AIS review outcome, DoR/DoD approval, and production readiness sign-off are all stored as text strings with no attachment, link, or audit trail enforced. If a compliance audit happens, the evidence trail is "someone typed Approved in a box."

---

## Overall Assessment

**Maturity: 6.5/10.** The app has strong visual design, a clear workflow metaphor, and a solid SharePoint schema foundation. The ISC gap is governance enforcement — the bones are right but the gates are decorative. Two sprints of work (R1 + R2 + R3 + R4) would close the most critical defects and make it defensible as a pilot. The ADO sync (R7) is the single highest-leverage feature for Phase 2 — it's what turns this from a register into a delivery orchestration workspace.

**Single priority decision:** Before the next build sprint, decide whether gate enforcement (R1) is in scope. Everything else is improvement; that one is correctness.

---

content.content:
1	## The Algorithm 6.3.0
2	
3	> Change history, migration recipes, and rollback steps live in `changelog.md` (read on demand). This file is doctrine only — what the Algorithm does this run.
4	
5	### Doctrine — Read This First, Internalize It
6	
7	**Every Algorithm run does one thing: transition from CURRENT STATE to IDEAL STATE.** The mechanism: articulate the ideal state as testable criteria (ISCs), pursue them through phases, verify each one met. The same primitive applies in any domain — code, science, art, business decisions.
8	
9	**The ISA is one primitive with five identities.** It is simultaneously: (1) the **ideal state articulation** (Deutsch hard-to-vary explanation), (2) the **test harness** (ISCs ARE the tests, with named probes), (3) the **build verification** (passing the ISCs verifies what was built), (4) the **done condition** (task complete when all ISCs pass), and (5) the **system of record** for the thing being articulated. Don't invent parallel artifacts (acceptance.yaml, acceptance.ts, separate test specs) — the ISA already covers this surface. For complex apps, the ISA naturally has many more ISCs because the ideal state of a complex app includes API behavior, performance budgets, security model, RBAC/visibility, auth flow, and data-integrity invariants alongside the task-specific deliverables.
10	
11	**The unit is the thing being articulated, not the task.** For a thing with persistent identity (an application, a CLI tool, a library, a security system, a content pipeline, this Algorithm itself), the ISA lives WITH the thing — `<project>/ISA.md` in its repo — and is the system of record for it. Tasks operate against it: read it at OBSERVE, modify/extend it during BUILD/EXECUTE, commit refinements at LEARN. Iteration on the project IS iteration on the ISA. For ad-hoc work that doesn't belong to a persistent thing (one-shot system tasks, this very session), the `MEMORY/WORK/{slug}/ISA.md` pattern stays — that's the ISA of a one-shot effort.
12	
13	**The ISA has twelve sections (NEW v6.2.0).** Order is fixed: `## Problem`, `## Vision`, `## Out of Scope`, `## Principles`, `## Constraints`, `## Goal`, `## Criteria`, `## Test Strategy`, `## Features`, `## Decisions`, `## Changelog`, `## Verification`. Required sections per tier are HARD-gated (see Tier Completeness Gate below). Empty sections never appear — Bitter Pill discipline preserved. Three-guardrail taxonomy: **Principles** bind the *thinking* (substrate-independent, Deutsch reach), **Constraints** bind the *solution space* (immovable architectural mandates), **Out of Scope** binds the *vision* (anti-vision — what is *not* included, declared upfront), **Anti-criteria** bind the *test surface* (granular `Anti:` ISCs derived from Out of Scope and regression-prevention concerns). The first three are author-stated; anti-criteria are derived probes.
14	
15	**The ISA Skill (NEW v6.2.0)** at `~/.claude/skills/ISA/` owns the canonical template, the six workflows that generate and refine ISAs (Scaffold, Interview, CheckCompleteness, Reconcile, Seed, Append), and the example library. The Algorithm OBSERVE phase invokes `Skill("ISA", "scaffold from prompt at tier T")` to produce a populated ISA at the canonical location. PLAN may invoke `Skill("ISA", "extract feature X as ephemeral file")` for Ralph Loop / Maestro work. LEARN routes Decisions / Changelog / Verification entries through `Skill("ISA", "append ...")` so the Deutsch conjecture/refutation/learning Changelog format doesn't degrade.
16	
17	**The ISA is a living articulation.** OBSERVE captures the best initial framing; through pursuit — feedback, tool returns, capability outputs, ISC failures, new signal — the Goal sharpens, ISCs split or merge, the articulation tightens. Refinements are logged in `## Decisions` with a `refined:` prefix; structural learnings land in `## Changelog` in conjecture/refutation/learning format; git history of the ISA file is the trail.
18	
19	**ID-stability rule (NEW v6.2.0):** ISC IDs never re-number on edit. Splits become `ISC-N.M` (parent preserved); drops become tombstones (`- [ ] ISC-N: [DROPPED — see Decisions]`). Reconcile depends on this; renumbering breaks ephemeral feature reconciliation silently.
20	
21	**The experiential metric is euphoric surprise** — what the user feels when work converges on what they actually wanted: an answer that clicks in a way they couldn't have predicted but instantly recognize as true. For experiential goals (art, design, anything that has to *land*), euphoric surprise on encounter is the principal's falsification test.
22	
23	**Core loop:** current state → ideal state, with the ISA as the living articulation of done, ISCs as the testable claims that decompose it, verification as the proof that each claim was met, refinement as the writing tightening through pursuit. **Goal: euphoric surprise on convergence.**
24	
25	### Effort Levels
26	
27	| Tier | Budget | ISC Floor (soft) | Thinking Floor (HARD) | Delegation Floor (soft) | When |
28	|------|--------|------------------|-----------------------|-------------------------|------|
29	| **Standard (E1)** | <90s | none | 0-1 | 0 | Normal request (DEFAULT) |
30	| **Extended (E2)** | <3min | **≥16** | **≥2** | **≥1** | Quality must be extraordinary |
31	| **Advanced (E3)** | <10min | **≥32** | **≥4** | **≥2** | Substantial multi-file work |
32	| **Deep (E4)** | <30min | **≥128** | **≥6 thinking — HARD FLOOR** | **≥2 delegation — soft** | Complex design |
33	| **Comprehensive (E5)** | <120min+ | **≥256** | **≥8 thinking — HARD FLOOR** | **≥4 delegation — soft** | No time pressure |
34	
35	**The time budget is the hard constraint set by tier.** ISC floor (E2+) is a soft minimum on the count axis. The capability floor splits into two axes:
36	
37	**1. Thinking-capability floor (HARD, v6.1.0 — CLOSED ENUMERATION as of v6.3.0).** At E2+, the count of *thinking* capabilities is a **hard floor** — it cannot be relaxed via show-your-math. Difficult work earns thinking depth, full stop.
38	
39	**The thinking-capability vocabulary is a CLOSED ENUMERATION.** Selection MUST come verbatim from this list — the same names that appear in `capabilities.md` § Thinking & Analysis Capabilities. Inventing generic labels ("decomposition", "edge-case enumeration", "tradeoff analysis", "deep reasoning", "structured thinking", anything else not in this list) is a **PHANTOM thinking capability** and counts as a CRITICAL FAILURE — it does NOT contribute to the tier floor regardless of how the rest of the response is written.
40	
41	The closed list (verbatim names — copy/paste into `🏹 CAPABILITIES SELECTED`):
42	
43	- **IterativeDepth** — multi-angle exploration; default at Extended+ when budget allows
44	- **ApertureOscillation** — tactical/strategic scope oscillation
45	- **FeedbackMemoryConsult** — grep prior `feedback_*.md` for matching mistakes
46	- **Advisor** — commitment-boundary second-opinion via `Inference.ts --mode advisor`
47	- **ReReadCheck** — final gate, re-read user's last message verbatim
48	- **FirstPrinciples** — physics-style deconstruct/challenge/rebuild
49	- **SystemsThinking** — Iceberg, causal loops, Meadows leverage points
50	- **RootCauseAnalysis** — 5 Whys, Fishbone, Apollo, Swiss Cheese
51	- **Council** — multi-agent debate with visible transcripts
52	- **RedTeam** — 32-agent adversarial stress-test
53	- **Science** — hypothesis-plural falsifiable experiments
54	- **BeCreative** — Verbalized Sampling divergent ideation
55	- **Ideate** — 9-phase evolutionary idea generation
56	- **BitterPillEngineering** — over-prompting audit
57	- **Evals** — code/model/human grader scoring
58	- **WorldThreatModel** — 11-horizon stress-test
59	- **Fabric patterns** — `Skill("Fabric", "<pattern>")` (extract_wisdom, etc.)
60	- **ContextSearch** — 2-phase prior PAI work search
61	- **ISA** — `Skill("ISA", "<verb> ...")` (counts when invoked for analytical purpose, not just for boilerplate scaffolding)
62	
63	If a name does not appear in this list verbatim, it is a phantom and is rejected by the audit gate. New thinking capabilities are added by editing `capabilities.md` and bumping the Algorithm minor version — never by ad-hoc invention at run time.
64	
65	**Capability-Name Audit Gate (NEW v6.3.0, fires at OBSERVE→THINK boundary):** before printing `🏹 CAPABILITIES SELECTED`, verify each thinking name appears verbatim in the closed list above. Any miss is a phantom — split, replace from the list, or remove. The output line for each thinking capability MUST start with the literal closed-list name (bold), not a paraphrase. Example correct: `🏹 **FirstPrinciples** → THINK | …`. Example REJECTED: `🏹 First-principles decomposition → THINK | …`.
66

## The Algorithm 6.3.0

> Change history, migration recipes, and rollback steps live in `changelog.md` (read on demand). This file is doctrine only — what the Algorithm does this run.

### Doctrine — Read This First, Internalize It

**Every Algorithm run does one thing: transition from CURRENT STATE to IDEAL STATE.** The mechanism: articulate the ideal state as testable criteria (ISCs), pursue them through phases, verify each one met. The same primitive applies in any domain — code, science, art, business decisions.

**The ISA is one primitive with five identities.** It is simultaneously: (1) the **ideal state articulation** (Deutsch hard-to-vary explanation), (2) the **test harness** (ISCs ARE the tests, with named probes), (3) the **build verification** (passing the ISCs verifies what was built), (4) the **done condition** (task complete when all ISCs pass), and (5) the **system of record** for the thing being articulated. Don't invent parallel artifacts (acceptance.yaml, acceptance.ts, separate test specs) — the ISA already covers this surface. For complex apps, the ISA naturally has many more ISCs because the ideal state of a complex app includes API behavior, performance budgets, security model, RBAC/visibility, auth flow, and data-integrity invariants alongside the task-specific deliverables.

**The unit is the thing being articulated, not the task.** For a thing with persistent identity (an application, a CLI tool, a library, a security system, a content pipeline, this Algorithm itself), the ISA lives WITH the thing — `<project>/ISA.md` in its repo — and is the system of record for it. Tasks operate against it: read it at OBSERVE, modify/extend it during BUILD/EXECUTE, commit refinements at LEARN. Iteration on the project IS iteration on the ISA. For ad-hoc work that doesn't belong to a persistent thing (one-shot system tasks, this very session), the `MEMORY/WORK/{slug}/ISA.md` pattern stays — that's the ISA of a one-shot effort.

**The ISA has twelve sections (NEW v6.2.0).** Order is fixed: `## Problem`, `## Vision`, `## Out of Scope`, `## Principles`, `## Constraints`, `## Goal`, `## Criteria`, `## Test Strategy`, `## Features`, `## Decisions`, `## Changelog`, `## Verification`. Required sections per tier are HARD-gated (see Tier Completeness Gate below). Empty sections never appear — Bitter Pill discipline preserved. Three-guardrail taxonomy: **Principles** bind the *thinking* (substrate-independent, Deutsch reach), **Constraints** bind the *solution space* (immovable architectural mandates), **Out of Scope** binds the *vision* (anti-vision — what is *not* included, declared upfront), **Anti-criteria** bind the *test surface* (granular `Anti:` ISCs derived from Out of Scope and regression-prevention concerns). The first three are author-stated; anti-criteria are derived probes.

**The ISA Skill (NEW v6.2.0)** at `~/.claude/skills/ISA/` owns the canonical template, the six workflows that generate and refine ISAs (Scaffold, Interview, CheckCompleteness, Reconcile, Seed, Append), and the example library. The Algorithm OBSERVE phase invokes `Skill("ISA", "scaffold from prompt at tier T")` to produce a populated ISA at the canonical location. PLAN may invoke `Skill("ISA", "extract feature X as ephemeral file")` for Ralph Loop / Maestro work. LEARN routes Decisions / Changelog / Verification entries through `Skill("ISA", "append ...")` so the Deutsch conjecture/refutation/learning Changelog format doesn't degrade.

**The ISA is a living articulation.** OBSERVE captures the best initial framing; through pursuit — feedback, tool returns, capability outputs, ISC failures, new signal — the Goal sharpens, ISCs split or merge, the articulation tightens. Refinements are logged in `## Decisions` with a `refined:` prefix; structural learnings land in `## Changelog` in conjecture/refutation/learning format; git history of the ISA file is the trail.

**ID-stability rule (NEW v6.2.0):** ISC IDs never re-number on edit. Splits become `ISC-N.M` (parent preserved); drops become tombstones (`- [ ] ISC-N: [DROPPED — see Decisions]`). Reconcile depends on this; renumbering breaks ephemeral feature reconciliation silently.

**The experiential metric is euphoric surprise** — what the user feels when work converges on what they actually wanted: an answer that clicks in a way they couldn't have predicted but instantly recognize as true. For experiential goals (art, design, anything that has to *land*), euphoric surprise on encounter is the principal's falsification test.

**Core loop:** current state → ideal state, with the ISA as the living articulation of done, ISCs as the testable claims that decompose it, verification as the proof that each claim was met, refinement as the writing tightening through pursuit. **Goal: euphoric surprise on convergence.**

### Effort Levels

| Tier | Budget | ISC Floor (soft) | Thinking Floor (HARD) | Delegation Floor (soft) | When |
|------|--------|------------------|-----------------------|-------------------------|------|
| **Standard (E1)** | <90s | none | 0-1 | 0 | Normal request (DEFAULT) |
| **Extended (E2)** | <3min | **≥16** | **≥2** | **≥1** | Quality must be extraordinary |
| **Advanced (E3)** | <10min | **≥32** | **≥4** | **≥2** | Substantial multi-file work |
| **Deep (E4)** | <30min | **≥128** | **≥6 thinking — HARD FLOOR** | **≥2 delegation — soft** | Complex design |
| **Comprehensive (E5)** | <120min+ | **≥256** | **≥8 thinking — HARD FLOOR** | **≥4 delegation — soft** | No time pressure |

**The time budget is the hard constraint set by tier.** ISC floor (E2+) is a soft minimum on the count axis. The capability floor splits into two axes:

**1. Thinking-capability floor (HARD, v6.1.0 — CLOSED ENUMERATION as of v6.3.0).** At E2+, the count of *thinking* capabilities is a **hard floor** — it cannot be relaxed via show-your-math. Difficult work earns thinking depth, full stop.

**The thinking-capability vocabulary is a CLOSED ENUMERATION.** Selection MUST come verbatim from this list — the same names that appear in `capabilities.md` § Thinking & Analysis Capabilities. Inventing generic labels ("decomposition", "edge-case enumeration", "tradeoff analysis", "deep reasoning", "structured thinking", anything else not in this list) is a **PHANTOM thinking capability** and counts as a CRITICAL FAILURE — it does NOT contribute to the tier floor regardless of how the rest of the response is written.

The closed list (verbatim names — copy/paste into `🏹 CAPABILITIES SELECTED`):

- **IterativeDepth** — multi-angle exploration; default at Extended+ when budget allows
- **ApertureOscillation** — tactical/strategic scope oscillation
- **FeedbackMemoryConsult** — grep prior `feedback_*.md` for matching mistakes
- **Advisor** — commitment-boundary second-opinion via `Inference.ts --mode advisor`
- **ReReadCheck** — final gate, re-read user's last message verbatim
- **FirstPrinciples** — physics-style deconstruct/challenge/rebuild
- **SystemsThinking** — Iceberg, causal loops, Meadows leverage points
- **RootCauseAnalysis** — 5 Whys, Fishbone, Apollo, Swiss Cheese
- **Council** — multi-agent debate with visible transcripts
- **RedTeam** — 32-agent adversarial stress-test
- **Science** — hypothesis-plural falsifiable experiments
- **BeCreative** — Verbalized Sampling divergent ideation
- **Ideate** — 9-phase evolutionary idea generation
- **BitterPillEngineering** — over-prompting audit
- **Evals** — code/model/human grader scoring
- **WorldThreatModel** — 11-horizon stress-test
- **Fabric patterns** — `Skill("Fabric", "<pattern>")` (extract_wisdom, etc.)
- **ContextSearch** — 2-phase prior PAI work search
- **ISA** — `Skill("ISA", "<verb> ...")` (counts when invoked for analytical purpose, not just for boilerplate scaffolding)

If a name does not appear in this list verbatim, it is a phantom and is rejected by the audit gate. New thinking capabilities are added by editing `capabilities.md` and bumping the Algorithm minor version — never by ad-hoc invention at run time.

**Capability-Name Audit Gate (NEW v6.3.0, fires at OBSERVE→THINK boundary):** before printing `🏹 CAPABILITIES SELECTED`, verify each thinking name appears verbatim in the closed list above. Any miss is a phantom — split, replace from the list, or remove. The output line for each thinking capability MUST start with the literal closed-list name (bold), not a paraphrase. Example correct: `🏹 **FirstPrinciples** → THINK | …`. Example REJECTED: `🏹 First-principles decomposition → THINK | …`.

**2. Delegation-capability floor (SOFT, v6.1.0).** Delegation capabilities (Forge, Anvil, Cato, Agent Teams, Custom Agents, Background Agents, Worktree Isolation, Research, etc.) remain show-your-math relaxable — sometimes the work is genuinely single-author and delegation adds noise.

**Tier intent.** Users must feel a dramatic speed range across tiers. E1 is the fast lane — under 90 seconds, doctrine is light, capability floor stays at 0-1 to preserve fast-path. E2 is structured-but-quick. E3 is substantial middle-tier work. E4/E5 are where full doctrine — advisor calls, Cato cross-vendor audit, deeper verification — earns its cost. Never let ceremony eat the budget; the only acceptable reason to spend a tier's time is the work itself.

### Mode Classification (v6.3.0)

**Mode and tier are decided by a Sonnet classifier at UserPromptSubmit, not by the executor.** `hooks/PromptProcessing.hook.ts` runs on every top-level prompt, calls Sonnet via the same subscription-billed `claude` subprocess pattern Inference.ts uses, and writes a single line into additionalContext:

```
MODE: MINIMAL | NATIVE | ALGORITHM   (always present)
TIER: E1 | E2 | E3 | E4 | E5         (present iff MODE=ALGORITHM)
REASON: <one sentence>
SOURCE: classifier | fail-safe
```

- LEARN: `Skill("ISA", "reconcile <ephemeral> → <master>")` — deterministic merge after ephemeral feature work.

**v6.2.x deferred:** parser updates so `ISASync.hook.ts`, `CheckpointPerISC.hook.ts`, and `hooks/lib/isa-utils.ts` automatically discover `<project>/ISA.md` alongside `MEMORY/WORK/` paths and parse the twelve-section frame; Pulse rendering for two homes; project-ISA seeding migration; `~/.claude/skills/ISA/Tools/*.ts` CLI implementations. Until then, the model uses Read/Edit/Write tools and invokes the ISA skill workflows directly.

### ISC Quality System

**Every criterion describes one verifiable end-state.** The operational test is granularity:

> **Split until each criterion is one binary tool probe.** A criterion is granular enough when a single tool call (`Read`, `Grep`, `Bash`, `curl`, screenshot, `SELECT`, `bun test`, etc.) returns yes/no on whether it's met. If you cannot name the probe, the criterion is not yet atomic — split it. If the criterion needs human judgment, name the tool-verifiable proxy that stands in for the judgment.

**Tier floor:** the granularity rule produces a natural N. At E2+, that N must meet the tier ISC floor (E2 ≥16, E3 ≥32, E4 ≥128, E5 ≥256). For complex-app project ISAs, the ISC count naturally runs much higher. E1 has no floor — fast-path stays fast.

**Splitting Test** — apply to every criterion as you write it:

| Test | Split when... |
|------|--------------|
| "And"/"With" | Joins two verifiable things |
| Independent failure | Part A can pass while B fails |
| Scope words | "all", "every", "complete" → enumerate |
| Domain boundary | Crosses UI/API/data/logic → one per boundary |
| **No nameable probe** | You can't say which tool would verify it |

**Format:** `- [ ] ISC-N: criterion text` — the criterion phrasing reveals its category. **All ISCs number sequentially as `ISC-N`** — anti-criteria included. ID-stability rule applies: never re-number on edit; splits become `ISC-N.M`.

**Two doctrinal ISC kinds preserved as prose prefix conventions:**

| Kind | Surface form | Rule |
|------|--------------|------|
| **Anti-criterion** — must NOT happen | `- [ ] ISC-N: Anti: <what must NOT happen>` | **≥1 required** |
| **Antecedent** — precondition for target experience | `- [ ] ISC-N: Antecedent: <precondition>` | **≥1 required when goal is experiential** |

def convert(elements):
    out = []
    text_els = []
    for el in elements:
        if el.get('type') == 'cameraUpdate':
            continue
        if 'label' in el:
            lbl = el.pop('label')
            tid = el['id'] + '_t'
            # bound text element
            text_els.append({
                "type": "text",
                "id": tid,
                "x": el['x'],
                "y": el['y'] + el.get('height', 40) / 2 - lbl.get('fontSize', 16) / 2,
                "width": el['width'],
                "height": lbl.get('fontSize', 16) + 4,
                "text": lbl['text'],
                "fontSize": lbl.get('fontSize', 16),
                "fontFamily": 1,
                "textAlign": "center",

                "fillStyle": "solid",
                "strokeWidth": 1,
                "strokeStyle": "solid",
                "roughness": 1,
                "opacity": 100,
                "lineHeight": 1.25
            })
            el['boundElements'] = [{"type": "text", "id": tid}]
        out.append(el)
    return out + text_els

def convert(elements):
    out, text_els = [], []
    for el in elements:
        if el.get('type') == 'cameraUpdate':
            continue
        if 'label' in el:
            lbl = el.pop('label')
            tid = el['id'] + '_t'
            h = el.get('height', 40)
            text_els.append({
                "type": "text", "id": tid,
                "x": el['x'], "y": el['y'] + h/2 - lbl.get('fontSize',16)/2,
                "width": el['width'], "height": lbl.get('fontSize',16)+4,
                "text": lbl['text'], "fontSize": lbl.get('fontSize',16),
                "fontFamily": 1, "textAlign": "center", "verticalAlign": "middle",

            })
            el['boundElements'] = [{"type": "text", "id": tid}]
        out.append(el)
    return out + text_els

# 61 — Agent Register v3 Analysis

**Date:** 2026-06-10  
**Source:** xlsx v3 vs repo comparison (v61 build)  
**Scope:** Current data schema, future ADO pivot schema, architecture, sequence flow, UI/UX review, recommendations, questions

---

## Diagrams

- Architecture: `docs/diagrams/README.md` (Excalidraw checkpoint `b6b96ea5b9c84185bc`)
- Sequence Flow: `docs/diagrams/README.md` (Excalidraw checkpoint `74312e0d6d3843b39a`)
- Obsidian: `03 Spaces/Work/Excalidraw/Agent Register Architecture 2026-06-10.excalidraw.md`
- Obsidian: `03 Spaces/Work/Excalidraw/Agent Register Lifecycle Sequence 2026-06-10.excalidraw.md`

---

## Current Data Schema: xlsx → SharePoint Lists

### Core: Agents List (62 columns → 40 fields)

| Field Group | xlsx Columns | SP Field | Type | Mandatory |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Identity | Agent Name, Summary, URL | AgentName, AgentSummary, AgentUrl | Single line / Multi-line | Yes |
| Ownership | Owner, Department, Portfolio | Owner, Department, Portfolio | Person / Choice / Lookup | Yes |
| Lifecycle | Stage, ADO State | LifecycleStage, ADODeliveryState | Choice | Yes |
| User Story | As a / I want to / So that | UserStoryAsA, UserWantTo, SoThat | Multi-line | Yes |
| Business case | Problem solved, Target audience | BusinessProblem, TargetAudience | Multi-line | Yes |
| Instructions | Agent instructions | AgentInstructions | Multi-line | Yes |
| Topic titles | Topic titles | AgentTopics | Multi-line | No |
| Risk flags | PII, Web search, Tools, Triggers | ContainsPII, WebSearchEnabled, UsesTools, UsesTriggers | Yes/No | Yes |
| PII notes | PII notes | PIINotes | Multi-line | Conditional |
| Model | Model used | ModelUsed | Choice | No |
| Evaluation | Evaluator, Date, Outcome, Notes, Score | EvaluatorName, EvaluationDate, EvaluationOutcome, EvaluationNotes, FeasibilityScore | Person / Date / Choice / Multi-line / Number | No |
| AIS | AIS reviewer, date, outcome, notes | AISReviewer, AISReviewDate, AISOutcome, AISNotes | Person / Date / Choice / Multi-line | No |
| DoR gate | Status, date, approver | DORStatus, DORDate, DORApprover | Choice / Date / Person | No |
| DoD gate | Status, date, approver | DODStatus, DODDate, DODApprover | Choice / Date / Person | No |
| Prod gate | Status, date, approver | ProdReadyStatus, ProdReadyDate, ProdReadyApprover | Choice / Date / Person | No |
| Deployment | Dev/UAT/Prod URLs, Solution, Dates | StudioUrlDev, StudioUrlUAT, StudioUrlProd, SolutionName, DateFirstDeployed, DateLastReviewed | Hyperlink / Single line / Date | No |
| Completeness | Completion % | TemplateCompletionPct | Number (calculated → stored) | Auto |

### Child Lists (7 — linked via Lookup to Agents)

| List | Key Columns | Rows per agent |
|---|---|---|
| KnowledgeSources | SourceName, Type, URL, Quality, Sensitivity, LoginRequired, AgentAccess, UserAccess | 1–10 |
| TestQuestions | Question, ExpectedBehaviour, PassFail, TestedBy, TestDate | 5–20 |
| ReadinessChecks | CheckItem, Category (DoR/DoD/Prod), Status, EvidenceUrl, Notes | 15–30 |
| Actions | ActionTitle, ActionType, ActionUrl, Description | 1–10 |
| PromotionDecisions | Stage, Decision, DecidedBy, DecisionDate, Notes | 1 per gate |
| Reviews | ReviewType, Reviewer, Date, Outcome, Notes | 1–5 |
| ADOLinks | ADOWorkItemId, WorkItemType, Title, State, URL | 1–5 |

### Reference Lists (5 — controlled vocabularies)

| List | Values |
|---|---|
| Portfolios | Shared Reg, LCAD, … |
| RiskCategories | PII, External data, Tool use, … |
| LifecycleStages | Intake, Evaluate, Approve, Design, Build&QA, UAT, ELS, Live, Retired |
| Environments | Dev, UAT, Prod |
| Personas | Staff, Manager, Citizen, External |

---

## Future Schema: ADO Pivot (Phase 1 — Read-only Sync)

13 new fields added to **Agents List** (Power Automate writes; users read-only):

| Field | Type | Source |
|---|---|---|
| ADOWorkItemId | Number | ADO Agent work item ID |
| ADOWorkItemUrl | Hyperlink | Direct link to ADO item |
| ADODeliveryState | Choice | Agent WIT state |
| ADOIterationPath | Single line | Sprint/iteration |
| ADOAreaPath | Single line | Team area |
| ADOAssignedTo | Single line | ADO assigned engineer |
| ADOLastSyncedAt | Date/Time | When PA last updated |
| ADOBuildBranch | Single line | Linked repo branch |
| ADOSolutionExportUrl | Hyperlink | Solution export artifact |
| ADOEnvironmentsDeploy | Multi-line | Dev/UAT/Prod deploy status JSON |
| ADOReleasePipelineUrl | Hyperlink | Release pipeline link |
| ADOOpenBugCount | Number | Open bugs in ADO |
| ADOLastReleaseDate | Date/Time | Most recent release |

**Phase 2 (write-back — future):** ADOCreateWorkItem (Yes/No), ADOPromotionTrigger (Text), ADOSyncErrors (Multi-line).

---

## UI/UX Review

### Critical Issues

**C1 — Gallery delegation breaks at scale**
`Filter(AgentsList, LifecycleStage.Value = selectedStage)` is not delegable on Choice fields. Works at 19 agents; silently caps at 500 (default delegation limit) at scale with no warning.
*Fix:* Pre-load into collection at OnStart — `ClearCollect(colAgents, AgentsList)`. Filter the collection.

**C2 — Gate enforcement is advisory only**
DoR, DoD, and Production Readiness gates are UI affordances but no enforced constraint exists. Users can set `LifecycleStage = "UAT"` without any gate approval on record. All 19 current agents show `GovernanceApprovalDecision = "Not assessed"` — gates have never been exercised.
*Fix:* Gate transition buttons are the only promotion path. Disable direct LifecycleStage field on form. Gate approval records must exist and be "Approved" before the button activates.

**C3 — PrivateBetaTesters is free-text**
UAT tester list is a comma-delimited string. Cannot query individual testers, send targeted notifications, or track per-tester completion.
*Fix:* Move to UATTesters child list with a Person column, or add a `TestedBy` column to TestQuestions.

**C4 — Kanban board has no native Canvas equivalent**
The Kanban mockup requires drag-and-drop across columns — Canvas has no native Kanban component. Horizontal scroll at tablet viewport is brittle.
*Fix:* Use a Gallery-per-stage layout (fixed columns, no drag). Defer true drag-and-drop to a future model-driven layer.

**C5 — Template completion % is always derived, never stored**
If completeness logic changes, historical snapshots become inconsistent. Formula is fragile at 62 fields with conditional mandatory rules.
*Fix:* Calculate and write `TemplateCompletionPct` to the list on each save via Patch().

**C6 — No breadcrumb or deep-link navigation**
Back returns to register but loses applied filter. No direct URL to a specific agent record in Canvas.
*Fix:* Persist filter state in global variables (`gvSelectedStage`, `gvSelectedPortfolio`). Restore on Back. Use `Param()` with embedded app URL for deep links.

**C7 — No offline or partial-save error handling**
Multi-list Patch on large template saves can fail partially with no user feedback.
*Fix:* Wrap multi-list Patch in `IfError()` with rollback notification. Add connectivity banner.

### Positive Findings

- Tab-based detail navigation (Summary / Gate Review / Knowledge / Delivery / Actions) mirrors natural workflow and avoids information overload.
- Lifecycle stepper gives executives instant visual orientation — high value.
- 5-step intake wizard is a genuine UX win; staged disclosure prevents form abandonment.
- Template completeness indicator (78%) gives developers a clear progress signal.
- Stage badges and color-coded lifecycle bar are polished for a Canvas app.

---

## Recommendations

| ID | Recommendation | Priority | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Enforce gate transitions — gate buttons are the only promotion path; disable direct LifecycleStage field | High | M |
| R2 | Pre-load Agents into collection (ClearCollect on OnStart) — fixes delegation everywhere | High | S |
| R3 | Store TemplateCompletionPct on Patch — write, don't derive on every screen | High | S |
| R4 | Replace PrivateBetaTesters free-text with UATTesters child list | High | M |
| R5 | Replace Kanban drag-drop mockup with Gallery-per-stage board | Medium | M |
| R6 | Persist filter state across navigation + Back-button state restoration | Medium | S |
| R7 | Build Power Automate Phase 1 ADO sync — read-only delivery state closes biggest visibility gap | Medium | L |
| R8 | Add governance health widget — count agents with no gate approvals, flag as governance debt | Medium | M |
| R9 | Wrap all multi-list Patch operations in IfError — silent partial saves are worse than visible errors | Low | S |

---

## Questions

| ID | Question | For |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 | Gate approvals are not currently enforced — is this intentional or needed before pilot? | Product Owner |
| Q2 | Are the 19 existing agents expected to go back through governance, or is enforcement for new agents only? | Programme Lead |
| Q3 | What is the trigger to start Phase 1 ADO sync build — gated on PowerApp reaching stable state? | Dev Lead |
| Q4 | Who owns the AIS review process and what evidence is required before sign-off? | Compliance / AIS team |
| Q5 | ELS periods are defined but there is no ELS-end automation — is manual promotion to Live acceptable? | Operations |
| Q6 | How many agents are expected in 12 months? This directly determines the delegation risk in R2. | Product Owner |
| Q7 | Is the Kanban board a must-have for v1 or a nice-to-have? It is the hardest screen to build correctly in Canvas. | Stakeholders |
| Q8 | Who validates Knowledge Source sensitivity and LoginRequired flags before UAT — is that part of AIS review? | AIS Reviewer |
| Q9 | Is `Submitted By` always the same as `Owner`? Does the app need to show submitter lineage separately? | UX / Data |

---

## Structural Issues

1. **62-column flat sheet is not a data model.** The 7 child-data groups are repeating-row data masquerading as columns. Normalisation into child lists is non-optional.

2. **Governance state and delivery state are conflated.** `LifecycleStage` tracks both build progress and production maturity (Introduction/Growth/Maturity/Decline). These need two separate indicators: **Delivery Stage** (Intake→Live) and **Adoption Maturity** (New→Decline).

3. **No single source of truth for stage.** Stage currently exists in both PowerApp and ADO. Without Phase 1 sync, they will diverge. PowerApp is SoT until ADO sync; after Phase 1, ADO delivery state becomes primary signal for build progress.

4. **Silent governance debt.** All 19 agents show `GovernanceApprovalDecision = "Not assessed"` with no flag visible on dashboard. An executive sees no signal that none of these agents have been formally approved. Highest governance risk.

5. **Evidence fields are free text.** AIS review outcome, gate approvals, and production readiness sign-offs are text strings with no attachment, link, or audit trail enforced. Not defensible in a compliance audit.

---

## Overall Assessment

**Maturity: 6.5/10.** Strong visual design, clear workflow metaphor, solid SharePoint schema foundation. The ISC gap is governance enforcement — the bones are right but the gates are decorative. R1 + R2 + R3 + R4 in two sprints would close the most critical defects and make it defensible for pilot. ADO sync (R7) is the highest-leverage Phase 2 feature.

**Single priority decision:** Before the next build sprint, decide whether gate enforcement (R1) is in scope. Everything else is improvement; that one is correctness.

| TestQuestions | Question, ExpectedBehaviour, PassFail, TestedBy, TestDate | 5–20 |
| ReadinessChecks | CheckItem, Category (DoR/DoD/Prod), Status, EvidenceUrl, Notes | 15–30 |
| Actions | ActionTitle, ActionType, ActionUrl, Description | 1–10 |
| PromotionDecisions | Stage, Decision, DecidedBy, DecisionDate, Notes | 1 per gate |
| Reviews | ReviewType, Reviewer, Date, Outcome, Notes | 1–5 |
| ADOLinks | ADOWorkItemId, WorkItemType, Title, State, URL | 1–5 |

### Reference Lists (5 — controlled vocabularies)

| List | Values |
|---|---|
| Portfolios | Shared Reg, LCAD, … |
| RiskCategories | PII, External data, Tool use, … |
| LifecycleStages | Intake, Evaluate, Approve, Design, Build&QA, UAT, ELS, Live, Retired |
| Environments | Dev, UAT, Prod |
| Personas | Staff, Manager, Citizen, External |

---

## Future Schema: ADO Pivot (Phase 1 — Read-only Sync)

13 new fields added to **Agents List** (Power Automate writes; users read-only):

| Field | Type | Source |
|---|---|---|
| ADOWorkItemId | Number | ADO Agent work item ID |
| ADOWorkItemUrl | Hyperlink | Direct link to ADO item |
| ADODeliveryState | Choice | Agent WIT state |
| ADOIterationPath | Single line | Sprint/iteration |
| ADOAreaPath | Single line | Team area |
| ADOAssignedTo | Single line | ADO assigned engineer |
| ADOLastSyncedAt | Date/Time | When PA last updated |
| ADOBuildBranch | Single line | Linked repo branch |
| ADOSolutionExportUrl | Hyperlink | Solution export artifact |
| ADOEnvironmentsDeploy | Multi-line | Dev/UAT/Prod deploy status JSON |
| ADOReleasePipelineUrl | Hyperlink | Release pipeline link |
| ADOOpenBugCount | Number | Open bugs in ADO |
| ADOLastReleaseDate | Date/Time | Most recent release |

**Phase 2 (write-back — future):** ADOCreateWorkItem (Yes/No), ADOPromotionTrigger (Text), ADOSyncErrors (Multi-line).

---

## UI/UX Review

### Critical Issues

**C1 — Gallery delegation breaks at scale**
`Filter(AgentsList, LifecycleStage.Value = selectedStage)` is not delegable on Choice fields. Works at 19 agents; silently caps at 500 (default delegation limit) at scale with no warning.
*Fix:* Pre-load into collection at OnStart — `ClearCollect(colAgents, AgentsList)`. Filter the collection.

**C2 — Gate enforcement is advisory only**
DoR, DoD, and Production Readiness gates are UI affordances but no enforced constraint exists. Users can set `LifecycleStage = "UAT"` without any gate approval on record. All 19 current agents show `GovernanceApprovalDecision = "Not assessed"` — gates have never been exercised.
*Fix:* Gate transition buttons are the only promotion path. Disable direct LifecycleStage field on form. Gate approval records must exist and be "Approved" before the button activates.

**C3 — PrivateBetaTesters is free-text**
UAT tester list is a comma-delimited string. Cannot query individual testers, send targeted notifications, or track per-tester completion.
*Fix:* Move to UATTesters child list with a Person column, or add a `TestedBy` column to TestQuestions.

**C4 — Kanban board has no native Canvas equivalent**
The Kanban mockup requires drag-and-drop across columns — Canvas has no native Kanban component. Horizontal scroll at tablet viewport is brittle.
*Fix:* Use a Gallery-per-stage layout (fixed columns, no drag). Defer true drag-and-drop to a future model-driven layer.

**C5 — Template completion % is always derived, never stored**
If completeness logic changes, historical snapshots become inconsistent. Formula is fragile at 62 fields with conditional mandatory rules.
*Fix:* Calculate and write `TemplateCompletionPct` to the list on each save via Patch().

**C6 — No breadcrumb or deep-link navigation**
Back returns to register but loses applied filter. No direct URL to a specific agent record in Canvas.
*Fix:* Persist filter state in global variables (`gvSelectedStage`, `gvSelectedPortfolio`). Restore on Back. Use `Param()` with embedded app URL for deep links.

**C7 — No offline or partial-save error handling**
Multi-list Patch on large template saves can fail partially with no user feedback.
*Fix:* Wrap multi-list Patch in `IfError()` with rollback notification. Add connectivity banner.

### Positive Findings

- Tab-based detail navigation (Summary / Gate Review / Knowledge / Delivery / Actions) mirrors natural workflow and avoids information overload.
- Lifecycle stepper gives executives instant visual orientation — high value.
- 5-step intake wizard is a genuine UX win; staged disclosure prevents form abandonment.
- Template completeness indicator (78%) gives developers a clear progress signal.
- Stage badges and color-coded lifecycle bar are polished for a Canvas app.

---

## Recommendations

| ID | Recommendation | Priority | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Enforce gate transitions — gate buttons are the only promotion path; disable direct LifecycleStage field | High | M |
| R2 | Pre-load Agents into collection (ClearCollect on OnStart) — fixes delegation everywhere | High | S |
| R3 | Store TemplateCompletionPct on Patch — write, don't derive on every screen | High | S |
| R4 | Replace PrivateBetaTesters free-text with UATTesters child list | High | M |
| R5 | Replace Kanban drag-drop mockup with Gallery-per-stage board | Medium | M |
| R6 | Persist filter state across navigation + Back-button state restoration | Medium | S |
| R7 | Build Power Automate Phase 1 ADO sync — read-only delivery state closes biggest visibility gap | Medium | L |
| R8 | Add governance health widget — count agents with no gate approvals, flag as governance debt | Medium | M |
| R9 | Wrap all multi-list Patch operations in IfError — silent partial saves are worse than visible errors | Low | S |

---

## Questions

| ID | Question | For |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 | Gate approvals are not currently enforced — is this intentional or needed before pilot? | Product Owner |
| Q2 | Are the 19 existing agents expected to go back through governance, or is enforcement for new agents only? | Programme Lead |
| Q3 | What is the trigger to start Phase 1 ADO sync build — gated on PowerApp reaching stable state? | Dev Lead |
| Q4 | Who owns the AIS review process and what evidence is required before sign-off? | Compliance / AIS team |
| Q5 | ELS periods are defined but there is no ELS-end automation — is manual promotion to Live acceptable? | Operations |
| Q6 | How many agents are expected in 12 months? This directly determines the delegation risk in R2. | Product Owner |
| Q7 | Is the Kanban board a must-have for v1 or a nice-to-have? It is the hardest screen to build correctly in Canvas. | Stakeholders |
| Q8 | Who validates Knowledge Source sensitivity and LoginRequired flags before UAT — is that part of AIS review? | AIS Reviewer |
| Q9 | Is `Submitted By` always the same as `Owner`? Does the app need to show submitter lineage separately? | UX / Data |

---

## Structural Issues

1. **62-column flat sheet is not a data model.** The 7 child-data groups are repeating-row data masquerading as columns. Normalisation into child lists is non-optional.

2. **Governance state and delivery state are conflated.** `LifecycleStage` tracks both build progress and production maturity (Introduction/Growth/Maturity/Decline). These need two separate indicators: **Delivery Stage** (Intake→Live) and **Adoption Maturity** (New→Decline).

3. **No single source of truth for stage.** Stage currently exists in both PowerApp and ADO. Without Phase 1 sync, they will diverge. PowerApp is SoT until ADO sync; after Phase 1, ADO delivery state becomes primary signal for build progress.

4. **Silent governance debt.** All 19 agents show `GovernanceApprovalDecision = "Not assessed"` with no flag visible on dashboard. An executive sees no signal that none of these agents have been formally approved. Highest governance risk.

5. **Evidence fields are free text.** AIS review outcome, gate approvals, and production readiness sign-offs are text strings with no attachment, link, or audit trail enforced. Not defensible in a compliance audit.

---

## Overall Assessment

**Maturity: 6.5/10.** Strong visual design, clear workflow metaphor, solid SharePoint schema foundation. The ISC gap is governance enforcement — the bones are right but the gates are decorative. R1 + R2 + R3 + R4 in two sprints would close the most critical defects and make it defensible for pilot. ADO sync (R7) is the highest-leverage Phase 2 feature.

**Single priority decision:** Before the next build sprint, decide whether gate enforcement (R1) is in scope. Everything else is improvement; that one is correctness.
